Task prompt
You are an expert AI assistant in breast pathology. You receive a pathology report and produce a concise interpretation and analysis for the attending pathologist. You do not reproduce or rewrite the report, and you do not replace the reporting pathologist or advise patients directly. Your output is read by the attending pathologist. Use precise, standard diagnostic terminology and abbreviations; interpret and analyse the report's findings rather than restating descriptions. Analyse the report using the sections below in the order given. Begin with CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS (discrepancies, internal inconsistencies, discordant or provisional findings, or specimen limitations; if none, state None). Give a one-line SPECIMEN. State the topline AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS. Give glanceable KEY FINDINGS (nodal ratio, largest deposit size, extranodal extension, nuclear grade, treatment response, RCB class, and biomarker status). Give an INTERPRETATION that integrates the nodal findings, extranodal extension, treatment response assessment, and RCB class into a complete staging and prognostic summary. End with RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES. Do not restate macroscopic or microscopic descriptions verbatim; fold the relevant findings into the interpretation. Apply the WHO Classification of Tumours: Breast Tumours, 5th edition, with AJCC 8th edition nodal staging. Assign the nodal stage and derive the overall pathological stage from the available data. Apply the Residual Cancer Burden system and state the RCB class. Where biomarker results are referenced but not present in this report, incorporate the most likely profile based on the nuclear grade and clinical context. Classify the primary tumour type based on the nodal morphology and available data. # Report 2605363 – Right axillary dissection – AI-assisted interpretation for the attending pathologist Source: `report_2605363_EN.pdf` (1 page; admission 04/29/2026, reported 05/05/2026; F, 41 y, outpatient). Anatomical pathology report only; no clinical history, prior biopsy result, or breast specimen is included in this accession. ## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS 1. **"RCB III" assigned on an axillary specimen alone is not derivable and should be treated as provisional.** RCB (Symmans/MDACC) is a composite breast + nodal index: RCB = 1.4(f_inv·d_prim)^0.17 + [4(1 − 0.75^LN)·d_met]^0.17; classes RCB-I ≤ 1.36, RCB-II 1.36–3.28, RCB-III > 3.28. Using this report's nodal data (LN = 26, d_met = 10 mm) the nodal term is **1.87** — effectively its ceiling for a 10 mm deposit (1 − 0.75^26 ≈ 0.999) and, by itself, in the **RCB-II** band. RCB-III requires a breast tumour-bed contribution with f_inv × d_prim > ~1.0 mm (e.g. 10 mm bed with > ~10 % invasive cellularity; 5 mm bed at 30 % → 3.37 = RCB-III; 20 mm bed at 5 % → 3.27 = RCB-II). If the breast shows pCR, the case is RCB-II (1.87). The final class must be computed after integration with the breast resection; the label "treatment response index … RCB III (no signs of treatment response)" also conflates a quantitative residual-disease index with qualitative therapy-effect assessment. 2. **Neoadjuvant therapy is implied (RCB / "treatment response" language) but nowhere documented.** No regimen, dates, pre-treatment cN, or M status. The "yp" prefix, the statement "no signs of treatment response", and the RCB assignment are all contingent on confirming NAT; untreated nodes are histologically indistinguishable from therapy-refractory nodes. 3. **Biomarkers referenced but absent.** "Performed on a prior study" — no ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 results, accession, date, or specimen type are cited. The receptor profile **cannot be inferred from nuclear grade**: grade 3 nuclei occur in TNBC, HER2-positive, and high-grade luminal B carcinomas alike; no profile is assumed in this analysis. The decision not to retest on residual disease merits reconsideration (see Recommendations) given the absence of any therapy effect and the subtype-dependence of post-neoadjuvant adjuvant options. 4. **Primary tumour not characterised in this report.** Deposits are described only as "carcinoma, nuclear grade 3". WHO 5th ed. histotype and Nottingham grade cannot be assigned from nodal morphology; "nuclear grade 3" must not be transcribed as histologic grade 3. Breast origin is presumed from context but is not explicitly stated, and the existence/location of the breast resection (concurrent, separate accession, or not yet performed) is not recorded. 5. **Specimen limitations.** Unoriented specimen → axillary levels (I/II/III, incl. level III/infraclavicular) not assignable. Status of the soft-tissue specimen edge relative to the 5 mm ENE is not stated (relevant to axillary RT planning). Not specified whether the 1 cm deposit measurement includes the extranodal component (no effect on N category). 6. **Minor internal inconsistencies.** Microscopy: "26 … show metastasis" (only the largest measured) vs. Diagnosis: "26 with macrometastasis" — the > 2 mm size of every deposit is not documented (does not alter ypN3a). Microscopy lists "foreign body reaction"; Diagnosis substitutes "cicatricial change" — the aetiology (prior SLNB/TAD, clip/marker, core biopsy, or therapy) is not addressed and retrieval of any clipped/marked node is not recorded. ## SPECIMEN Right total axillary lymph node dissection (ALND), unoriented 12 × 8 × 6 cm fibroadipose fragment in formalin, 50 LNs (up to 1.5 cm) in 19 blocks; presumed post-neoadjuvant setting; no breast specimen in this accession. ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Metastatic high-grade (nuclear grade 3) carcinoma, presumed breast primary, in 26 of 50 right axillary lymph nodes (macrometastases, largest 10 mm) with extranodal extension up to 5 mm and no histological therapy effect — **ypN3a (AJCC 8th)**, residual nodal disease/non-pCR; anatomic stage IIIC (any T, N3, M0) pending ypT and M; **RCB class not determinable from this specimen** (nodal component 1.87; reported RCB-III provisional pending breast tumour-bed data). ## KEY FINDINGS - **Nodal ratio:** 26/50 positive (LNR 0.52; 52 %) → ypN3a (≥ 10 positive axillary nodes, ≥ 1 deposit > 2 mm; threshold exceeded > 2.5-fold). - **Largest deposit:** 10 mm (1.0 cm) — macrometastasis. - **Extranodal extension:** present, up to 5 mm (> 2 mm; extensive category). Soft-tissue edge status not reported. - **Nuclear grade:** 3 in nodal deposits (Nottingham grade not assessable on nodes). - **Treatment response:** none identified in the evaluated nodes (no regression described). Soft tissue: fat necrosis, foreign-body reaction, scarring — aetiology unspecified. - **RCB class:** report states RCB-III "for this dissection"; nodal term calculates to 1.87 (RCB-II band alone); final class requires breast tumour bed (d1 × d2, % invasive cellularity, % in situ) → **provisional**. - **Biomarker status:** not performed on this specimen; prior ER/PR/HER2 (± Ki-67) referenced but not reported → unknown in this report. - **Other:** 41-year-old female (premenopausal age range); 6-day turnaround (04/29 → 05/05/2026). ## INTERPRETATION **Nodal burden and ENE.** Twenty-six macrometastatic nodes with a 10 mm largest deposit place this axilla firmly in the highest AJCC nodal category (ypN3a, or pN3a if no NAT was given). Level III involvement would independently satisfy N3a but cannot be evaluated in an unoriented specimen; it does not change the category. ENE is not a staging variable in AJCC 8th but is a recognised adverse locoregional factor; at 5 mm it exceeds the customary 2 mm cut-off and, together with a LNR of 0.52, marks a high axillary recurrence risk and informs regional nodal irradiation planning. Whether tumour reaches the soft-tissue edge of the specimen is unstated and clinically relevant. **Stage.** Under AJCC 8th, any T with N3 and M0 is **anatomic stage IIIC**, so the stage group is fixed at IIIC irrespective of the ypT category (ypT0–ypT4) provided cM0; if M1 was established before NAT the case remains stage IV regardless of response. ypT must be taken from the breast resection. This is not a pCR (pCR requires ypT0/is ypN0). The AJCC 8th prognostic stage group is designed for upfront-surgery patients and in any case requires Nottingham grade and ER/PR/HER2 — none available here — so the post-therapy stage should be reported as anatomic ypTNM, with the pre-treatment clinical prognostic stage retained alongside. **Treatment response.** If NAT is confirmed, the complete absence of therapy effect across 26 involved nodes indicates a chemoresistant phenotype. Residual nodal disease after NAT, particularly at the N2–N3 level, carries a worse prognosis than the equivalent nodal category in an untreated axilla, and this is compounded by grade 3 nuclei, ENE, high LNR, and young age. **RCB.** The nodal contribution (1.87) is already at its maximum for a 10 mm deposit, so the reported class hinges entirely on the breast: virtually any measurable residual invasive primary (f_inv × d_prim > ~1 mm) yields RCB-III, whereas a breast pCR yields RCB-II. RCB-III is the class with the highest distant-relapse and mortality risk in all receptor subtypes; RCB-II with this nodal profile would still be high-risk. Either way, residual disease is extensive and the case requires subtype-directed post-neoadjuvant systemic therapy and comprehensive locoregional management — decisions that depend on the missing biomarker profile. Note also that if an SLNB/TAD preceded NAT (a possible explanation for the fat necrosis/foreign-body reaction/scar), RCB and ypN are assessed on the post-therapy ALND alone and the pre-therapy nodal findings must be recorded separately. **Primary tumour type and biomarkers.** WHO 5th ed. histotype cannot be classified from this report; the deposits are compatible with, but not specific for, high-grade IBC-NST (statistically the most likely type in the absence of documented special-type features), and lobular/special types are not excluded because no architecture or IHC is described. Breast origin is presumed from the clinical context (prior biomarker study) and should be confirmed. No receptor profile is assumed: nuclear grade does not predict ER/PR/HER2 status with clinically usable accuracy. ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES 1. **Integrate with the breast resection** (same or separate accession): ypT, residual tumour-bed d1 × d2, % invasive cellularity, % in situ → compute the formal RCB index (MDACC calculator) and confirm or correct the "RCB III" class; report a single combined RCB for the case. 2. **Confirm clinical history:** NAT regimen and completion date; pre-treatment cTNM (cN, imaging nodal burden) and M status (cM0 vs pre-NAT M1); prior axillary procedures (SLNB/TAD), biopsy-clip placement, and whether the marked node was retrieved (specimen radiograph if applicable) — correlate with fat necrosis/foreign-body reaction/scar. 3. **Retrieve and cite the prior biomarker results** (ER, PR, HER2 IHC ± ISH, Ki-67; accession, date, specimen type) in this report. **Consider retesting on residual nodal disease** — adequate FFPE substrate — particularly if prior results were negative/equivocal, obtained on a limited core, or if heterogeneity is suspected; post-NAT receptor discordance is well documented and the adjuvant pathway for residual disease is subtype-dependent. 4. **Confirm breast origin and histotype/Nottingham grade** from the prior core/breast specimen (WHO 5th ed.). Only if a primary is unavailable: IHC on the nodal deposit (GATA3, TRPS1, mammaglobin, GCDFP-15, ER; E-cadherin/p120 if lobular is considered; CK7/CK20 to exclude non-mammary origin). 5. **Complete CAP/ICCR nodal elements:** macro- vs micrometastasis breakdown for all 26 nodes; ENE extent category (> 2 mm) and whether the 10 mm measurement includes extranodal tumour; soft-tissue specimen-edge status relative to ENE; explicit statement that levels are not assignable (unoriented) — communicate to surgeon/radiation oncologist. 6. **Add a formal staging line:** ypN3a (AJCC 8th); anatomic stage IIIC (any T, N3, M0) pending ypT and M; note prognostic stage group not applicable post-NAT; retain pre-treatment clinical stage. 7. **MDT/clinical flags:** age 41 meets germline testing criteria by age alone (≤ 50 y) irrespective of subtype; high-risk residual disease → subtype-directed post-neoadjuvant therapy and comprehensive regional nodal RT planning.

Level III involvement would qualify as N3a by itself but cannot be assessed here. - ypN3b/c cannot be assessed because the internal mammary (IMN) and supraclavicular basins were not sampled. - With a 50-node yield, LNR 0.52 means more than half the nodal basin is involved: high-volume residual nodal disease. - 0.52 falls in the intermediate band (0.21–0.65) of published LNR schemes. # Pathology Report Analysis — Request No. 2605363 **Specimen received 04/29/2026 · Reported 05/05/2026 · Female, 41 y · Outpatient** --- ## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS 1. **RCB class is not derivable from this specimen.** The RCB index is a *case-level* composite requiring the bidimensional residual tumour bed size (d_prim), % overall invasive cellularity and % in situ component (f_inv) from the **breast** specimen, in addition to the nodal terms. This accession contains axillary tissue only. On the nodal data alone (LN = 26, d_met = 10 mm), the nodal term computes to ≈1.87 — **below the RCB-III threshold of >3.28**. RCB-III becomes mathematically valid only once a primary-tumour term >1.41 is added (i.e. f_inv × d_prim ≳ 1.0; e.g. a 30 mm tumour bed with ≥4% residual invasive cellularity). The report's own wording — "treatment response index **for this dissection**" — concedes this. **Recommend re-issuing the RCB class as provisional, or as an addendum after the breast specimen is integrated.** Clinically RCB-III is highly probable, but as currently stated it is unsupported by the data in this accession. 2. **Neoadjuvant therapy is implied but never documented.** RCB assignment and "no signs of treatment response" presuppose a post-neoadjuvant setting, yet no regimen, treatment dates, or pre-treatment cT/cN are recorded. Without this, the **"yp" prefix cannot be formally applied** and post-therapy prognostic tools (CPS+EG) cannot be scored. 3. **No breast specimen / no ypT.** Overall pathological stage cannot be finalised from this accession. Clarify whether the primary was resected in a separate/prior accession or remains in situ (a delayed, isolated axillary dissection). 4. **No biomarker data in this accession.** The comment defers ER/PR/HER2 to a prior study. This is defensible for diagnosis but **debatable for management**: in chemorefractory residual disease, repeat ER/HER2 on the residual deposit carries direct therapeutic consequence (T-DM1 eligibility if HER2+; HER2-low reclassification; capecitabine/olaparib pathways if HER2−). At minimum, the prior results must be transcribed into this report so the synoptic is not left biomarker-blank. 5. **Internal tension between "no treatment response" and the stromal findings.** Fat necrosis, foreign-body giant-cell reaction and cicatricial change are documented in perinodal soft tissue, yet nodal therapy effect is reported as absent. Confirm these represent procedural/clip-site or fat-necrosis change rather than under-recognised nodal regression (hyalinised fibrosis, mucin pools, foamy macrophage aggregates). The distinction is material to RCB, as treated nodes with fibrous scar but no viable tumour are scored as negative. 6. **Grading is incomplete for classification purposes.** Only **nuclear grade 3** is given, derived from metastatic deposits. A Nottingham (Elston–Ellis) histologic grade cannot be assigned from nodal metastases, and post-NAC grading of the primary is itself of limited validity. Do not report the nuclear grade as an overall histologic grade. 7. **Deposit measurement vs. ENE.** Node size on macroscopy (up to 1.5 cm) and largest metastasis (1.0 cm) are distinct parameters and are not in conflict — but confirm the 10 mm figure is the largest *contiguous metastatic deposit* (the value required by both AJCC and RCB) and that the 5 mm extranodal component was recorded separately rather than folded into it. 8. **Specimen not oriented; Berg levels not separable.** N category is unaffected (≥10 positive nodes = pN3a regardless), but apical/level III status cannot be stated — relevant to regional nodal irradiation field design. 9. **Minor:** the signature block renders as "[ANONYMIZED PATHOLOGIST ? ONCOLOGIST]" (character corruption); verify the authenticated signatory line. --- ## SPECIMEN Right total axillary lymph node dissection (50 nodes, 19 blocks); no breast/primary tumour tissue submitted in this accession. --- ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS **Extensive macrometastatic involvement of the right axilla (26/50 nodes) by nuclear grade 3 invasive carcinoma, most consistent with invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), with extranodal extension and no histologic evidence of neoadjuvant treatment effect — (y)pN3a; anatomic Stage IIIC (M0 assumed), pending ypT. Chemorefractory residual disease; RCB-III as stated by the reporting pathologist, to be finalised on the breast specimen.** --- ## KEY FINDINGS | Parameter | Result | |---|---| | **Nodal ratio** | **26/50 positive (LNR 0.52)** — node yield well above adequacy standards | | **Largest deposit** | **10 mm** (macrometastasis; all involved nodes reported as macrometastatic) | | **Extranodal extension** | **Present**, up to **5 mm** beyond the capsule into perinodal soft tissue | | **Nuclear grade** | **3** (high grade); Nottingham grade not assignable from nodal tissue | | **Treatment response** | **None identified** in nodes (no regressive fibrosis/acellular tumour bed described) | | **RCB class** | **RCB-III** per report — *axillary component only; nodal term ≈1.87 in isolation; requires breast specimen to validate* | | **Biomarker status** | **Not performed on this specimen**; deferred to prior study — ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 **absent from this report** | | **Other** | Fat necrosis, foreign-body reaction, cicatricial change in soft tissue; 24 nodes uninvolved | --- ## INTERPRETATION The axillary content defines a **high-burden, chemoresistant nodal phenotype**. Twenty-six involved nodes places this unequivocally in **AJCC 8th edition N3a** (≥10 positive axillary nodes with at least one deposit >2.0 mm); the 10 mm largest deposit independently confirms macrometastatic disease and excludes the micrometastasis/ITC categories. Because the report invokes treatment response, the category is properly rendered **ypN3a** once neoadjuvant administration is documented. With M0, **any ypT combined with N3 yields anatomic Stage IIIC**; this is the ceiling of locoregional staging and is insensitive to primary tumour size, so the missing ypT does not alter the anatomic stage group — only the ypT descriptor and the AJCC *prognostic* stage group remain outstanding. The prognostic stage group requires ER/PR/HER2 and grade: a grade 3, HR+/HER2− or triple-negative profile holds the case at Stage IIIC, whereas a favourable ER+/PR+/HER2+ profile can downstage it under the AJCC 8th pathological prognostic tables — a further reason the biomarker set must be reconciled into this report. The **extranodal extension of 5 mm** is an adverse modifier that does not change the N category in breast carcinoma but materially affects management. It exceeds the 2 mm threshold used in most axillary-management and radiotherapy datasets, correlates with residual nodal burden beyond the dissected field, and, in combination with N3a disease, is a firm indication for comprehensive post-mastectomy/regional nodal irradiation including supraclavicular and internal mammary consideration. The absence of specimen orientation prevents a statement on level III/apical involvement, which should be conveyed to radiation oncology as a planning uncertainty rather than a negative finding. The **treatment-response assessment is the dominant prognostic driver**. Complete absence of regressive change across 26 involved nodes, with retained nuclear grade 3 morphology, indicates intrinsic chemoresistance rather than partial cytoreduction. Post-neoadjuvant nodal status is the strongest surviving prognostic variable in this setting, and ypN3a with no response occupies the poorest stratum: event-free and overall survival are substantially inferior to any pCR or low-RCB outcome, and the risk is front-loaded to the first three years. The scarring, fat necrosis and foreign-body reaction in perinodal fat are most plausibly procedural (biopsy/clip site) or degenerative, and should not be over-read as therapy effect — but they warrant deliberate exclusion of subtle nodal regression before "no response" is finalised, since converting even a few nodes to "treated/negative" would lower both the LN count and the RCB index. Regarding **RCB**, the index as reported must be read as an **axillary-only, provisional estimate**. Substituting LN = 26 and d_met = 10 mm into the nodal term gives approximately 1.87, which falls in the RCB-II range; the class advances to RCB-III only when the breast tumour-bed term is added. Given that any measurable residual primary with even minimal cellularity pushes the composite past 3.28, **RCB-III is the expected final class**, but it should be issued as such only in an integrated report or addendum that records d_prim, % invasive cellularity and % in situ. RCB-III concordantly identifies the group with the least benefit derived from neoadjuvant therapy and the greatest need for escalated adjuvant systemic treatment. On **tumour typing**, the metastases are described as cohesive macrometastatic deposits of nuclear grade 3 carcinoma, without the discohesive, single-file or signet-ring morphology that would suggest a lobular primary, and without micropapillary, mucinous or apocrine features. On the available morphology the primary is best classified as **invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), high grade**, per WHO 5th edition; this remains provisional pending review of the primary. As to the **likely biomarker profile**, a grade 3 tumour showing complete chemorefractoriness with massive nodal burden is most compatible with **HR-positive/HER2-negative, luminal B-like biology**, in which low pCR rates and RCB-III outcomes predominate; triple-negative disease is less likely given that non-response is the minority behaviour in that subtype, but if present it would carry the most adverse implication and would open the capecitabine pathway. HER2-positive disease is the least likely but the **most consequential to miss**, since unresponsive HER2+ residual disease is a direct indication for adjuvant T-DM1. This uncertainty is precisely why the deferral of repeat biomarker testing should be revisited. At 41 years the patient is presumptively premenopausal, which bears on ovarian function suppression and on germline testing thresholds. --- ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES 1. **Integrate the breast specimen** (same or prior accession) to establish ypT, tumour bed bidimensional dimensions, % overall invasive cellularity and % in situ component; recompute the RCB index formally (MD Anderson calculator) and issue the definitive class by addendum. Complete the full ypTNM and AJCC 8th prognostic stage group. 2. **Document neoadjuvant details** — regimen, cycles, start/stop dates, pre-treatment cT/cN by imaging and core biopsy — to license the "yp" prefix and to permit **CPS+EG scoring**, which meaningfully refines prognosis in ypN3 residual disease. 3. **Retrieve and transcribe prior ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 and the original histologic type and Nottingham grade** into this report so the synoptic is complete. 4. **Reconsider repeat ER/PR/HER2 (ASCO/CAP-compliant IHC ± reflex ISH) on the residual nodal metastasis.** Chemorefractory residual disease has a non-trivial receptor-discordance rate, and the result is actionable: T-DM1 (KATHERINE) if HER2+; capecitabine (CREATE-X) if HER2−/TNBC; HER2-low status for future T-DXd eligibility. Select the block containing the 10 mm deposit. 5. **Level-sections ± pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3) on nodes showing fibrous scar or hyalinisation**, to confirm that "no treatment response" is accurate and that no treated/regressed nodes have been miscategorised. Routine IHC on morphologically uninvolved nodes is not otherwise indicated given established macrometastases. 6. **E-cadherin ± p120 catenin** if re-review of the metastatic deposits shows any discohesive or single-file pattern, to exclude an invasive lobular primary. 7. **Confirm retrieval of the clipped/marked node** and verify laterality concordance with the right breast primary; clarify whether levels I–III were all submitted despite the absence of orientation. 8. **Germline BRCA1/2 and multigene panel testing** — age 41 with high-grade, high-burden residual disease; also determines **olaparib (OlympiA)** eligibility in HER2− high-risk residual disease. 9. **Systemic staging** (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with bone scan, or FDG PET-CT) to exclude occult M1 disease before adjuvant planning, given N3a burden with extranodal extension. 10. **Multidisciplinary tumour board referral** for escalated adjuvant systemic therapy and for radiotherapy planning (comprehensive regional nodal irradiation, with the level III/apical and internal mammary uncertainty explicitly communicated). 11. Genomic recurrence-risk assays (Oncotype DX/MammaPrint) are **not indicated** in node-positive residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy. --- *Interpretive analysis generated to support the attending pathologist; not a substitute for the authenticated diagnostic report. All conclusions are limited to the material and data contained in accession 2605363.*

CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS - Methodological limitation: RCB class assigned as RCB III based solely on axillary dissection (50 LNs, 26 positive) without primary breast tumor bed parameters (tumor bed size, cellularity, % DCIS). Formal RCB per Symmans et al. cannot be calculated from nodal material alone; current RCB III should be qualified as extensive residual nodal disease / nodal-only RCB equivalent. - Specimen limitation: Unoriented irregular adipose fragment 12x8x6 cm, 50 LNs up to 1.5 cm processed in 19 blocks (>1 LN/block). Potential undersampling for micrometastases/ITC and subtle treatment response. No pT available for overall staging. - Interpretive nuance: Soft tissues described as fat necrosis, foreign body reaction, and cicatricial change, yet microscopic assessment states no signs of treatment response. Requires clinical correlation to exclude iatrogenic/post-biopsy change vs therapy effect. No regression fibrosis, foamy macrophages, or other therapy-related histology reported in nodes. - Staging dependency: Overall pathological stage cannot be fully derived from nodal dissection alone without primary tumor pT and clinical M. pN category alone drives stage. - None other; 26 macrometastases clearly documented, ENE documented. SPECIMEN Right axillary lymph node dissection, unoriented (admission 04/29/2026, Report 05/05/2026, Req 2605363, 41-year-old female): 12 x 8 x 6 cm adipose tissue, 50 LNs dissected, 19 blocks. AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Metastatic invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), nuclear grade 3, involving axillary nodes - 26 of 50 nodes with macrometastasis, largest deposit 1.0 cm, extranodal extension present up to 5 mm, no histologic evidence of treatment response, compatible with nodal residual burden RCB III / chemoresistant disease - ypN3a (pN3a if de novo) - at least Stage IIIC if M0 pending pT. KEY FINDINGS - Nodal ratio: 26/50 positive = 52%, all macrometastases per report (largest 1.0 cm / 10 mm, >2 mm threshold for macro). - Largest deposit size: 1.0 cm (10 mm) metastasis; nodes up to 1.5 cm gross. - Extranodal extension (ENE): Present, perinodal soft tissue involvement up to 5 mm - extensive ENE (>2 mm) per AJCC 8th prognostic factor, CAP reporting element. - Nuclear grade: Grade 3 carcinoma in nodal metastases (high-grade, poor differentiation). - Treatment response: No signs of treatment response observed in evaluated nodes per diagnosis; no tumor bed fibrosis, necrosis, or histiocytic response attributed to therapy. - RCB class: Reported as RCB III (no signs of treatment response) - extensive residual disease, chemoresistant category; however calculation is nodal-only, not full RCB. - Biomarker status: Not performed on current sample per Comments ("biomarkers were performed on a prior study"). Inferred most likely high-grade basal-like triple-negative phenotype (ER-/PR-/HER2-) or HER2-enriched high-grade carcinoma based on nuclear grade 3, age 41, extensive nodal burden, and lack of treatment response. Definitive profile requires review of prior biomarker report. If primary is invasive carcinoma NST grade 3, Nottingham grade 3 equivalent. INTERPRETATION This is an extensive axillary disease burden specimen: Right axillary dissection without orientation yielding 50 LNs, 26 with metastatic carcinoma of nuclear grade 3. By WHO Classification of Breast Tumours 5th edition, nodal morphology of high-grade carcinoma with no special features documented is most consistent with invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), grade 3 (ductal type). Lobular phenotype not suggested; verification with primary tumor histology required. AJCC 8th edition nodal staging: ≥10 positive ipsilateral axillary nodes = pN3a. With 26 positive nodes, category is pN3a. In post-neoadjuvant setting (implied by RCB reporting attempt), designation is ypN3a, with 26 ypN+ and extensive treatment-resistant disease. All deposits are macrometastases (>2 mm), largest 10 mm. ENE present with perinodal soft tissue involvement 5 mm meets criteria for extensive extranodal extension, adverse prognostic factor for locoregional recurrence and survival, does not upstage N per AJCC but is mandatory CAP/AJCC prognostic element. Treatment response and Residual Cancer Burden: Histologically no regression changes in nodes. In post-neoadjuvant context this indicates lack of nodal response. Reported as RCB III - by Symmans criteria, RCB III = extensive residual disease, poor prognosis, chemoresistant. True RCB requires primary tumor bed cellularity, dimensions, and in situ percentage in addition to nodal number/size of largest metastasis. With nodal-only data, RCB III here reflects high residual nodal burden (26 nodes, 1 cm largest deposit) consistent with RCB-III category clinically, but not a validated total RCB score. Staging synthesis: Without breast specimen, pT = pTX. Assuming M0, with pN3a, overall pathological stage is at least pStage IIIC (AJCC 8th: any T N3 M0 = IIIC; T1-3 N3a = IIIC) if invasive primary present. If no prior NAT, pN3a. If post-NAT, ypN3a consistent with ypStage IIIC residual disease. Prognostically, nodal ratio 52%, 26 macrometastatic nodes, extensive ENE to 5 mm, nuclear grade 3, and RCB III imply high risk of distant metastasis and poor disease-free/overall survival. Fat necrosis and foreign body giant cell reaction with cicatricial change in axillary soft tissue likely reflects prior intervention (biopsy/surgery) rather than therapy effect given pathologist interpretation. RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES - Correlate with clinical history: Confirm neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) status, regimen (chemotherapy +/- anti-HER2), timing, and clinical/radiologic response to validate yp vs p staging and appropriateness of RCB reporting. - Retrieve and review prior breast primary pathology and prior biomarker report referenced in Comments: histologic type, Nottingham grade, ER/PR/HER2 IHC and HER2 ISH if equivocal, Ki-67%. Given nuclear grade 3, most likely triple-negative breast carcinoma (TNBC) NST or HER2-positive high-grade carcinoma; do not repeat without indication but ensure prior report is available in case. - If no prior biomarkers available or if clinically indicated (e.g., initial core was triple-negative/HER2-low, or long interval), consider biomarker retesting on nodal metastasis (ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67) per ASCO/CAP guidelines for metastatic recurrence, with appropriate controls. - Confirm M status clinically; document overall AJCC 8th prognostic stage once pT from breast surgery is available, or cT from clinical exam/imaging if breast not resected. Requires multidisciplinary tumor board discussion given pN3a / ypN3a RCB-III. - Report ENE extent (5 mm) in synoptic format as extensive ENE >2 mm; consider comment on margin/soft tissue involvement status for radiation planning. - No additional levels/IHC needed on current axillary material unless occult micrometastases questioned, given already extensive positivity; however ensure adequate sampling documentation for 50 nodes in 19 blocks meets CAP adequacy.

SPECIMEN Right axillary dissection (12 × 8 × 6 cm; 50 nodes in 19 blocks), post-treatment (yp), 41-year-old woman. AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS ypN3a (AJCC 8th) residual high-grade invasive carcinoma NST, 26/50 axillary macrometastases with 5 mm ENE, no nodal treatment effect, RCB III; overall ypStage IIIC (ypTX ypN3a, M not assessed on this specimen). KEY FINDINGS - Nodal ratio: 26/50 (52%); all reported as macrometastases → ypN3a - Largest deposit: 10 mm - ENE: present, 5 mm (extensive, >2 mm) - Nuclear grade: 3 - Treatment response: none in evaluated nodes - RCB class: III (extensive residual disease) - Biomarkers: not performed on this sample (prior study cited, results not provided). Most likely profile given NG3 plus chemo-resistant residual burden: ER-positive / HER2-negative, luminal B-like; confirm on the prior report (TNBC and HER2+ remain possible but less typical of zero nodal response). INTERPRETATION This is a post-neoadjuvant right axillary clearance with heavy residual nodal disease. The 10 mm largest deposit and 5 mm extranodal extension indicate established macrometastatic, extensively extra-capsular disease; ENE does not upstage beyond N3a in breast AJCC 8th but is an adverse locoregional risk factor. Absence of treatment effect in involved nodes, together with RCB III assigned on this dissection, indicates chemo-resistant residual cancer. The lymph-node RCB component alone (LN = 26, dmet = 10 mm) is sufficient for the extensive-residual (RCB-III) range even without a scored primary bed. Fat necrosis and cicatricial/foreign-body change in surrounding soft tissue are not interpreted as nodal regression. Prognostically this is unfavourable residual disease: high nodal ratio, N3a, extensive ENE, high nuclear grade, and RCB III. In a 41-year-old woman this residual burden warrants multidisciplinary review for adjuvant systemic intensification, regional RT planning (axilla/SCF), and restaging as clinically indicated. Mammary origin requires primary-tumour correlation; the supplied nodal description does not establish a specific WHO (5th edition) breast carcinoma histotype. ## KEY FINDINGS | Parameter | Finding | |---|---| | Nodal burden | **26/50** nodes with macrometastases; ratio **0.52 (52%)** | | Largest metastatic deposit | **10 mm (1 cm)** | | Extranodal extension | Present; perinodal soft-tissue involvement **up to 5 mm** | | Nuclear grade | **3**; Nottingham grade not established | | Treatment response | No histological treatment response identified in evaluated nodes | | RCB | **Class III, as reported; not independently validated** | | Biomarkers | Prior profile referenced; ER, PR, HER2 and Ki-67 results unavailable here | ## INTERPRETATION For a breast primary, the 26 macrometastatic axillary nodes meet **AJCC 8th-edition pN3a** criteria; use **ypN3a** if neoadjuvant systemic therapy is confirmed. Extranodal extension is an adverse feature but does not change the N3a category. Primary pT/ypT is unavailable. Primary treatment (fit patient, presumed uterus-confined disease) - **Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy** by a **minimally invasive approach**, avoiding any intraperitoneal tumour spillage or morcellation; peritoneal survey. # Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary - Request No. 2605694 (report_2605694_EN) **Source data (as printed in the report):** female, 47 years, outpatient; admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026. Three samples: Block 1 "Endocervix" (0.5 cc mucohemorrhagic material), Block 2 "Endometrium" (3 cc mucohemorrhagic material), Block 3 "Endometrial polyps" (1 cc, multiple light brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces). The microscopic section reads only "See diagnosis". The report contains no IHC or molecular results, no imaging, no description of myometrium and no clinical history (menopausal status, fertility wishes, BMI, family history). The material is fragmentary and described by volume. The procedure is not named, and "RESECTION" in the heading does not denote a hysterectomy specimen. **Bottom line:** Low-grade (FIGO grade 2) endometrioid adenocarcinoma on limited, fragmentary samples. Stage, myometrial depth, cervical involvement and molecular subgroup are all undetermined, so no risk group can be assigned yet. "FIGO II" in the diagnosis is the histological **grade**, not stage II. ## DIAGNOSIS: **Endometrioid-pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma (endometrioid carcinoma), moderately differentiated - FIGO grade 2** (reported as "FIGO II"). This is low-grade in the binary scheme used by FIGO 2023 and ESGO-ESTRO-ESP, where G1-G2 = low-grade. - Reported (specimen: "ENDOCERVIX, ENDOMETRIUM, ENDOMETRIAL POLYPS, RESECTION (3 SAMPLES)"): "ENDOMETRIOID PATTERN ENDOMETRIAL ADENOCARCINOMA, MODERATELY DIFFERENTIATED, FIGO II, WITHOUT EVIDENCE OF VASCULONEURAL INVASION IN THIS SAMPLE." - "FIGO II" follows directly after "moderately differentiated" and is the grade (by definition 6-50% non-squamous solid growth). The report does not give the solid-growth percentage or nuclear grade. - "Some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement" (Block 3). The report does not itemise carcinoma by block beyond this. - Adequacy comments: "No normal endocervix identified"; "scarce representation of basal endometrium." ## FIGO STAGE: **Cannot be definitively assigned - insufficient data. The report states no stage, and none should be inferred from it ("FIGO II" is not stage II).** - Surgical stage requires a hysterectomy specimen (plus nodal/adnexal assessment) to establish myometrial depth, cervical stroma, LVSI extent, serosa/adnexa and nodes. Here there are only fragmentary samples, no myometrium described, and no imaging or operative findings. - Cervical stromal involvement can be neither shown nor excluded. No normal endocervix was identified in the endocervical sample, and carcinoma in that sample is not described. There is therefore no basis for stage II (cervical stromal invasion). - Planning assumption only (not a stage): presumed uterus-confined disease (clinical stage I), substage undeterminable. This reflects limited sampling, not proven absence of invasion. - How the final FIGO 2023 stage will be set (low-grade endometrioid = non-aggressive histotype): - confined to polyp/endometrium: IA1 - <50% myometrial invasion, no/focal LVSI: IA2 - >=50% myometrial invasion, no/focal LVSI: IB - cervical stromal invasion: IIA - substantial LVSI (>=5 vessels): IIB - extra-uterine spread or nodal disease: III-IV - Once molecular data exist: POLEmut stage I-II becomes IAmPOLEmut; p53abn with myometrial invasion becomes IICmp53abn. ## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification): **Cannot be assigned from the available material.** - The report only *suggests* IHC on Block 3 (Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2). No results are reported. Therefore p53-abnormal and MMR-deficient cannot be called. POLE-ultramutated cannot be evaluated either, because POLE exonuclease-domain sequencing is not part of the suggested panel. - NSMP must not be assigned by default. It is a diagnosis of exclusion (non-pathogenic POLE, retained MMR expression, wild-type p53), and none of these has been tested. - Of the suggested markers, only MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 and p53 are classifier tests. ER is needed to refine NSMP. P16, PR, beta-catenin and keratin cocktail are ancillary, and the report does not state their purpose. ## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION: **Absent in this sample** ("without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample"). - Caveats: - "Vasculoneural" does not separate lymphovascular from perineural invasion. - LVSI cannot be reliably excluded on fragmentary biopsy/curettage-type material. - Focal vs substantial LVSI is staging-relevant (FIGO 2023 IIB) and must be assessed on the hysterectomy specimen. ## MYOMETRIAL INVASION: **Not assessable - no depth can be estimated.** - No myometrium is described in the submitted material (mucohemorrhagic material and tissue fragments only; basal endometrium scarcely represented). The report gives no depth or percentage (no <50% / >=50% statement), so any figure would be speculation. - To be determined pre-operatively by pelvic MRI or expert ultrasound, and definitively on the hysterectomy specimen. ## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES: Reported: - Endometrioid histotype (a FIGO 2023 "non-aggressive" histological type). - Moderately differentiated, grade 2 (low-grade). - No vasculoneural invasion in this sample. - Adenocarcinoma in polypoid fragments. Extent is unknown, and disease confined to a polyp/endometrium (IA1) cannot be confirmed on fragments. Unknown, and these will decide the risk group: - Myometrial depth, cervical stromal involvement, LVSI extent, and adnexal/serosal/nodal status. - Molecular subgroup and ER status, the strongest missing determinants: - POLEmut: favourable. - p53abn: high risk. - MMRd and NSMP: intermediate. ER-negative NSMP is treated as higher risk in the 2025 ESGO-ESTRO-ESP update. - MMRd would also trigger Lynch syndrome evaluation. - Limited sampling: grade and histotype from fragments may be revised on the hysterectomy specimen. - Patient factors: age 47 years; menopausal status, fertility wishes, BMI, comorbidities and family history are not provided. Provisional impression: favourable histology (low-grade endometrioid), but no formal risk group can be assigned yet. ## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT: Stage and molecular subgroup are both undetermined, so management is stepwise and conditional. The frame is FIGO 2023 and the ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 guideline update, which are external to the report. Decisions should be made at a multidisciplinary tumour board. 1. **Complete the pathology work-up now** (Block 3 as suggested, or the block with the most viable tumour): - MMR IHC (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), p53 IHC and ER (>=10% = positive) +/- PR, plus P16, beta-catenin and keratin cocktail as proposed. - Add POLE exonuclease-domain sequencing, which is not in the suggested panel. The guideline allows omitting it only in low-risk stage I disease, where it would not change adjuvant therapy; that cannot be judged yet. - Equivocal p53: TP53 sequencing. MLH1 loss: MLH1 promoter methylation. MMRd without methylation, or suspicious family history: genetic counselling and germline testing for Lynch syndrome. - Assign the subgroup by the hierarchy POLE, then MMR, then p53, then NSMP. For multiple classifiers, POLEmut + MMRd/p53abn is classed as POLEmut, and MMRd + p53abn as MMRd. - If tumour is scant or results are equivocal, repeat on the hysterectomy specimen. - Request a pathology addendum quantifying solid growth, nuclear grade and tumour amount. 2. **Clinical and imaging staging:** - Pelvic MRI (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) for myometrial invasion, cervical stromal involvement and adnexa/pelvic nodes. Block 1 cannot answer the cervical question. # Tumour Board Diagnostic Summary: Endometrial Carcinoma **Report:** `report_2605694_EN.pdf`, Anatomical Pathology Report (Histological Study), Request No. 2605694 **Patient:** female, 47 years, outpatient. Admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026 (dates as printed). **Evidence base:** this one-page report is the only source. No imaging, operative, IHC/molecular, family-history or other clinical data were provided. I used FIGO 2023, the WHO 5th edition classification and the ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 guidelines only to interpret the report and to frame recommendations. Nothing from those sources is presented as a finding in this patient. ## Report findings (as documented) | Block | Label | Macroscopic description | |---|---|---| | 1 | "Endocervix" | Mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 0.5 cc | | 2 | "Endometrium" | Mucohemorrhagic material, combined volume 3 cc | | 3 | "Endometrial polyps" | Multiple light brown tissue fragments with raw surfaces, combined volume 1 cc | - **Microscopic description:** "See diagnosis." There is no separate microscopic text. - **Diagnosis** (one combined diagnosis under "ENDOCERVIX, ENDOMETRIUM, ENDOMETRIAL POLYPS, RESECTION (3 SAMPLES)"): - "Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, FIGO II, without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample" - "Some polypoid fragments with adenocarcinoma involvement" - "No normal endocervix identified" - "Scarce representation of basal endometrium" - **Comment:** immunohistochemistry is *suggested* on Block 3: Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2. **No IHC results are reported, and no addendum was provided.** > **Key interpretive points** > 1. **"FIGO II" is the FIGO grade, not the FIGO stage.** It appears next to "moderately differentiated", which means FIGO grade 2. It does not mean stage II. > 2. **The specimen is fragmented resection/curettage material, not a hysterectomy.** A surgical stage and the depth of myometrial invasion cannot be derived from it. > 3. **IHC was only recommended, so the molecular subgroup cannot be assigned.** POLE testing was not requested at all. > 4. **"No normal endocervix identified" means the endocervical sample is not representative, so cervical status is unknown.** This finding is *not* evidence of cervical stromal invasion. --- ## DIAGNOSIS: **Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2 (moderately differentiated).** Under FIGO 2023, grade 1–2 endometrioid carcinoma is low grade and counts as a "non-aggressive" histological type. - Adenocarcinoma involves some of the polypoid (endometrial polyp) fragments. - Other statements in the report: - no vasculoneural invasion in this sample - no normal endocervix identified - scarce basal endometrium - **Limitations:** - There is no microscopic description. The architectural basis for grade 2 is therefore not documented. By FIGO definition, grade 2 means 6–50% solid non-squamous, non-morular growth. - Apart from the polyp fragments, the report does not say which of the three samples contain carcinoma. - The suggested p53/p16/ER/PR panel would also help confirm the endometrioid histotype and an endometrial rather than endocervical origin. This matters because no normal endocervix was identified. - Histotype and grade should be confirmed on the hysterectomy specimen. ## FIGO STAGE: **Cannot be assigned from the available material. The surgical-pathological FIGO stage is undetermined, and no "most likely" stage can responsibly be named from this specimen.** Reasons: 1. **"FIGO II" does not mean stage II.** In the report it follows "moderately differentiated" and describes FIGO grade 2. Recording stage II would wrongly imply cervical stromal invasion and could lead to overtreatment, such as radical surgery or radiotherapy. 2. **FIGO staging (2009 and 2023) is surgical-pathological.** It needs hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) and nodal staging to define: - depth of myometrial invasion - cervical stromal invasion - extent of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI): focal, or substantial (≥5 vessels) - adnexal, serosal, nodal and peritoneal status FIGO 2023 also builds in histotype, grade, LVSI and molecular class (e.g., IAm POLEmut, IICm p53abn). None of this information is available. 3. **Cervical involvement is neither shown nor excluded.** - No normal endocervix was identified. - The report does not state that carcinoma is present in the "Endocervix" sample. - Carcinoma fragments in an endocervical sample could be displaced tumour from the uterine body. They would not prove cervical *stromal* invasion, which is the only cervical finding that defines stage II (FIGO 2023 IIA). Under FIGO 2009, involvement of endocervical glands alone is still stage I. 4. **What can be said:** - Carcinoma involves the endometrium and endometrial polyps. - No reported finding documents cervical stromal invasion, substantial LVSI or disease outside the uterus. - This is *compatible with* stage I but does not establish it. - For a low-grade endometrioid tumour, the final FIGO 2023 stage could be anything from IA1 (confined to a polyp or the endometrium) through IA2, IB, IIA and IIB to III–IV. It would carry a molecular annotation, e.g., IAm POLEmut, or IICm p53abn if the tumour is p53-abnormal with any myometrial invasion. ## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification): **Cannot be assigned from the available material.** IHC (p53, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 and the rest of the panel) was only suggested on Block 3; it was not performed or reported. POLE mutation analysis was not requested. - None of the four subgroups (POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal, NSMP) can be named. - **NSMP must not be assigned by default.** It is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires POLE wild-type, MMR-proficient and p53 wild-type results. - Low-grade endometrioid morphology does not predict the subgroup; all four subgroups can look like this. - **Tests needed to classify:** - p53 IHC - MMR IHC (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation testing if MLH1 or MLH1/PMS2 expression is lost - **POLE exonuclease-domain sequencing covering all 11 pathogenic variants.** This is not in the suggested panel and cannot be done by IHC. - If more than one classifier is abnormal, classify by the genomic driver: POLEmut takes precedence over MMRd, and MMRd over p53abn. - **Supporting biomarkers (refine prognosis but do not define the subgroup):** - ER status: ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 splits NSMP into "low-grade and ER-positive" versus "high-grade and/or ER-negative". - Nuclear β-catenin: a surrogate for CTNNB1 mutation and an adverse factor within low-grade NSMP. ## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION: **Absent: not identified in this sample.** The report says "without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample". "Vasculoneural" covers lymphovascular and perineural invasion. - **This finding is provisional.** It is based on small fragments without myometrium or the tumour–myometrium interface, which is where LVSI is usually seen. - Definitive LVSI status and its extent (none, focal, or substantial = ≥5 vessels by WHO criteria) must be assessed on the hysterectomy. Substantial LVSI would upstage a low-grade endometrioid tumour to FIGO 2023 IIB. ## MYOMETRIAL INVASION: **Not assessable. The depth cannot be estimated from this specimen.** - None of the three samples is described as containing myometrium. - The report explicitly notes "scarce representation of basal endometrium", so even the endometrial–myometrial junction is barely sampled. - As a result, none of these categories can be inferred: - no invasion (IA1) - invasion of less than 50% (IA2) - invasion of 50% or more (IB) - **Absence of invasion must not be assumed from this biopsy.** - Next steps: - Pre-operative estimate: pelvic MRI or expert transvaginal ultrasound. - Definitive depth and its ratio to myometrial thickness: measured on the hysterectomy specimen. ## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES: | Feature | Status from report | Effect on risk | |---|---|---| | Histotype | Endometrioid | Non-aggressive type (FIGO 2023); favourable | | Grade | FIGO grade 2 (moderately differentiated) | Low grade; favourable | | LVSI | Not identified in this sample | Favourable but provisional | | Polyp involvement | Some polypoid fragments involved | Stage IA1 only if confined to polyp/endometrium on hysterectomy; not proven | | Age | 47 years | Under 60, which matters for de-escalation if risk is intermediate. Diagnosis before 50 is a classic Lynch syndrome warning sign. | | Molecular subgroup | **Unknown** | Main driver of risk: POLEmut makes stage I–II disease low risk; p53abn with any myometrial invasion becomes IICm p53abn (high risk) | | ER/PR, β-catenin | **Unknown** | NSMP that is ER-negative with myometrial invasion is high risk despite low grade | | Depth of myometrial invasion | **Unknown (not assessable)** | Separates IA from IB | | Cervical stromal invasion | **Unknown** (no normal endocervix) | Would define IIA | | LVSI extent (focal vs substantial) | **Unknown** | Substantial would mean IIB | | Adnexa, serosa, nodes, peritoneum | **Unknown** (no staging or imaging) | Would define stage III–IV | - **Sampling limitations:** - fragmented material (0.5 cc, 3 cc and 1 cc) - no myometrium - scarce basal endometrium - no normal endocervix - no separate microscopic description - no block-by-block distribution of the carcinoma - biopsy grade and histotype can change on the hysterectomy - **ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 risk group: cannot be allocated.** Allocation needs both the FIGO 2023 stage and the molecular subgroup. The recommended sequence is: complete the molecular classification, stage the disease surgically, then treat according to the integrated risk group. **1. Complete the pathology now (on Block 3, or Block 2 if Block 3 has too little tumour)** - Perform the suggested IHC: p53, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, ER, PR and β-catenin, plus p16 and keratin cocktail as diagnostic aids. - **Add POLE mutation testing.** - ESGO 2025 allows it to be omitted only in low-risk stage I disease, where the result would not change adjuvant treatment. - The stage is unknown, so testing is warranted. - A POLE wild-type result is also needed before a tumour can be called NSMP, or before p53abn can be accepted as the driver. - The result decides treatment if final pathology shows stage IB, cervical stromal invasion, substantial LVSI or p53abn with myometrial invasion; in those cases a POLE mutation would allow de-escalation to no adjuvant treatment. - Test MLH1 promoter methylation if MLH1 (with or without PMS2) expression is lost. - Molecular testing on curettage material is valid and encouraged. It becomes relevant if the tumour proves p53-abnormal with advanced or recurrent disease, or if the histotype is revised to serous carcinoma or carcinosarcoma (ESGO 2025). **2. Pre-operative work-up** - History: family history of Lynch-associated cancers, menopausal status, comorbidities and reproductive wishes. - Pelvic and speculum examination. - Pelvic MRI (preferred here, to assess cervical stromal involvement and myometrial depth) or expert transvaginal ultrasound. - Chest imaging. Primary surgery (for presumed uterus-confined disease)** - **Standard operation:** total (simple) hysterectomy with BSO and sentinel lymph node biopsy (indocyanine green by cervical injection, with ultrastaging of the nodes). - A minimally invasive approach is preferred. - Avoid morcellation and tumour spillage. - If sentinel nodes do not map, perform side-specific lymphadenectomy for high-intermediate or high risk, and consider it for intermediate risk. - **Omentectomy:** not needed for endometrioid histology. - **Radical hysterectomy:** not indicated because of "FIGO II", which is a grade, not a stage. # Diagnostic summary — Request No. 2605694 Source: anatomical pathology report, outpatient histological study. Female, 47 years. Admission 05/07/2026; report date 05/11/2026. Specimens (resection, 3 samples): endocervix (mucohemorrhagic material, 0.5 cc, Block 1); endometrium (mucohemorrhagic material, 3 cc, Block 2); endometrial polyps (multiple light brown fragments with raw surfaces, 1 cc, Block 3). Microscopic description: “See diagnosis.” No hysterectomy, myometrium, adnexa, lymph nodes, or completed biomarker results are in this report. ## DIAGNOSIS Endometrioid-pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, FIGO grade II. No normal endocervix is identified, so cervical involvement cannot be determined from the specimen label alone. Carcinoma involving polypoid fragments does not establish confinement to a polyp or justify stage IA. ## MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification) **Cannot be assigned.** Immunohistochemistry was only suggested on **Block 3**; no results are reported. The recommended panel comprises **Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2**. There is also no reported POLE mutation analysis. Consequently, none of **POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal, or NSMP** can be established. Endometrioid morphology alone does not establish NSMP. ## LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION **Absent/not identified in the examined sample**, with the report specifically stating **“without evidence of vasculoneural invasion in this sample.”** This limited-sample finding does not definitively exclude lymphovascular invasion elsewhere in the tumour. ## MYOMETRIAL INVASION **Not assessable; neither depth in millimetres nor percentage invasion can be estimated.** Basal endometrium is scarcely represented, and no myometrial tissue, endomyometrial interface, or full-thickness uterine wall assessment is documented. Absence of invasion cannot be inferred. ## KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES - Established **endometrioid histology and FIGO grade 2**, with adenocarcinoma involving some polypoid fragments. - No vascular/neural invasion identified in the submitted material, subject to limited sampling. - Fragmentation and scarce basal endometrium prevent assessment of tumour confinement and invasion depth. - Cervical stromal involvement, tumour size, nodal status, extrauterine extent, and molecular subgroup are undetermined. **A definitive prognostic risk group cannot be assigned** without adequate staging pathology and molecular results. ## RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT 1. **Gynaecological-oncology/tumour-board assessment for definitive management and staging.** If clinically suitable, plan definitive surgery with adequate uterine pathological assessment; myometrial depth, cervical stromal involvement, LVSI, and any nodal/extrauterine disease require evaluation. # Diagnostic summary — report 2605694 **DIAGNOSIS:** Endometrioid-pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated (**FIGO grade 2**). Adenocarcinoma involves some endometrial polyp fragments. **FIGO STAGE:** **Cannot be assigned** from these fragmented endocervical, endometrial and polyp specimens. The report's “FIGO II” accompanies the differentiation/grade description; it does **not** establish surgical stage II. Myometrial invasion, cervical stromal involvement, nodal status and extrauterine spread are not assessable from the report. No normal endocervix was identified. **MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition):** **Indeterminate.** p53 and mismatch-repair IHC (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) were *suggested* for block 3, not reported as performed; no POLE result is provided. POLE-ultramutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal and NSMP cannot be distinguished. **LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION:** **Not identified in the submitted sample** (reported as no evidence of “vasculoneural invasion”). Absence throughout the tumour cannot be confirmed on this limited material. **MYOMETRIAL INVASION:** **Depth cannot be estimated.** No evaluable myometrium or invasion depth is reported; basal endometrium is only scantily represented. Polyp involvement does not establish myometrial invasion. **KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES:** Endometrioid-pattern, grade 2 carcinoma with involvement of polyp fragments; vascular invasion was not seen in these samples. Risk stratification is limited by unknown myometrial depth, extent of LVSI in the whole tumour, cervical/nodal/extrauterine status and molecular subgroup. **RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT:** Refer to gynaecologic oncology for definitive staging and treatment. If operable, consider total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and appropriate sentinel lymph-node assessment; evaluate the resection for myometrial and cervical stromal invasion, LVSI and extrauterine disease. Perform MMR and p53 IHC on suitable tumour tissue (block 3 was suggested) and POLE sequencing if feasible to establish the integrated molecular subgroup. **A stage- and molecular-specific adjuvant recommendation is not possible yet.** If final findings indicate low-risk uterine-confined disease, observation may suffice; higher-risk anatomical findings, substantial LVSI or a p53-abnormal profile may warrant radiotherapy and/or systemic therapy, while early-stage POLE-ultramutated disease may allow de-escalation. Decide adjuvant treatment at the tumour board using final stage and molecular results.

# DIAGNOSTIC SUMMARY & TUMOUR BOARD REPORT **Reference:** Pathology Report No. 2605694 | **Patient Age:** 47 years (Female) **Specimen:** Resection / sampling of Endocervix (Block 1), Endometrium (Block 2), and Endometrial polyps (Block 3) --- ### DIAGNOSIS: - **Histological Type:** Endometrioid pattern endometrial adenocarcinoma (involving endometrial tissue and polypoid fragments). - **Histological Grade:** FIGO Grade II (moderately differentiated). --- ### FIGO STAGE: - **Status:** **Cannot be definitively assigned from the available material.** - **Reasoning:** - Endometrial cancer staging according to FIGO criteria (FIGO 2009 / 2023) is a surgical and pathological staging system requiring evaluation of a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimen, along with nodal and peritoneal assessment. - The submitted specimen consists entirely of curettage/biopsy and polypectomy fragments (endocervix 0.5 cc, endometrium 3 cc, endometrial polyps 1 cc). - Essential staging parameters cannot be determined: 1. *Depth of myometrial invasion:* Only a "scarce representation of basal endometrium" is present; no full-thickness myometrial wall is available to determine whether the tumor is confined to the endometrium, invades <50% of the myometrium (Stage IA), or invades ≥50% of the myometrium (Stage IB). 2. *Cervical involvement:* The endocervical sample contained only mucohemorrhagic material with "no normal endocervix identified," precluding evaluation of cervical stromal invasion (Stage II). 3. *Extrauterine and nodal status:* Adnexal, serosal, parametrial/vaginal, peritoneal, and pelvic/paraaortic lymph node statuses (Stage III/IV) are unassessed. - If disease is ultimately confined to the uterine corpus upon surgical resection, the most likely eventual surgical stage is Stage I (IA or IB), but definitive staging requires completion of primary surgical resection. --- ### MOLECULAR SUBGROUP (WHO 5th edition integrated classification): - **Status:** **The molecular subgroup cannot be assigned from the available material.** - **Reasoning:** - According to the WHO 5th edition integrated classification and ESGO/ESTRO/ESP guidelines, endometrial carcinomas are categorized into four distinct molecular subgroups: 1. *POLE-ultramutated (POLEmut)* 2. *Mismatch repair-deficient (MMR-deficient / MMRd)* 3. *p53-abnormal (p53abn)* 4. *No specific molecular profile (NSMP)* - In this report, immunohistochemistry (IHC) was only recommended/suggested by the pathologist ("On Block 3, immunohistochemistry studies are suggested, especially to determine biomarker profile including Keratin Cocktail, P53, P16, Estrogen Receptors, Progesterone Receptors, Beta-Catenin, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2") and was **not performed**. - No molecular/sequencing testing for *POLE* exonuclease domain mutations was performed. - Because no IHC results or molecular data are reported, the tumor cannot be categorized into any of the four WHO molecular subgroups at this time. --- ### LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION: - **Absent.** - **Report Details:** The pathology report explicitly states "WITHOUT EVIDENCE OF VASCULONEURAL INVASION IN THIS SAMPLE." (Definitive status will be confirmed on the final hysterectomy specimen). --- ### MYOMETRIAL INVASION: - **Status:** **Cannot be assessed / Insufficient data to determine depth.** - **Reasoning:** The received specimen consists solely of superficial curettage and polypectomy fragments (endocervix, endometrium, and endometrial polyps). The microscopic evaluation specifically notes a "scarce representation of basal endometrium" with no underlying myometrium included. Evaluation of the presence and depth of myometrial invasion (<50% vs ≥50%) requires histological examination of the full-thickness uterine wall from a hysterectomy specimen. --- ### KEY PROGNOSTIC FEATURES: 1. **Histological Type and Grade (Favorable to Intermediate):** - Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is a type I endometrial carcinoma associated with a generally more favorable prognosis than non-endometrioid histotypes (e.g., serous, clear cell, or carcinosarcoma). - FIGO Grade II (moderately differentiated) places the tumor in an intermediate-grade category, carrying a higher recurrence risk than FIGO Grade I, but lower than FIGO Grade III. 2. **Absence of Lymphovascular / Vasculoneural Invasion (Favorable):** - Vasculoneural/lymphovascular invasion (LVSI) is not identified in the examined tissue, which is a favorable prognostic factor against early nodal dissemination, pending confirmation on the surgical resection specimen. 3. **Patient Age (47 years):** - Relatively young, pre/perimenopausal patient. Although younger age (<50 years) is associated with favorable baseline survival, the presence of a Grade II carcinoma standardly necessitates surgical staging. 4. **Critical Missing / Pending Prognostic Parameters:** - *Depth of Myometrial Invasion:* The primary driver of T-stage and local recurrence risk (<50% vs ≥50%) is currently unknown. - *Cervical Stromal Invasion:* Unassessed ("no normal endocervix identified"). - *Nodal Status:* Preoperative/unassessed. - *Molecular Subgroup:* Crucial for modern risk stratification under WHO 5th edition / ESGO-ESTRO-ESP guidelines. Identification of *POLE* mutation confers an excellent prognosis, MMR-deficiency indicates intermediate prognosis and triggers Lynch syndrome evaluation, while p53-abnormality shifts the tumor into a high-risk category warranting intensified adjuvant therapy. - *Hormone Receptor Status:* ER/PR expression remains pending (suggested in the IHC panel). --- ### RECOMMENDED MANAGEMENT: 1. **Immediate Diagnostic & Pathology Workup:** - **Perform Suggested Immunohistochemistry (Block 3):** Carry out the suggested IHC panel, specifically MMR proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), p53, and ER/PR to establish the molecular subgroup and Lynch syndrome screening status. Consider *POLE* mutation sequencing if indicated by institutional algorithm. - **Preoperative Staging Imaging:** Obtain a pelvic MRI with contrast (or expert transvaginal ultrasound) to estimate depth of myometrial invasion and assess for cervical involvement, alongside chest/abdominal imaging (CT scan) to rule out extrauterine disease or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. 2. **Primary Surgical Treatment (Standard of Care):** - **Procedure:** Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TH/BSO), preferably performed via a minimally invasive approach (laparoscopic or robotic-assisted). - **Nodal Assessment:** Sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping and biopsy with pathological ultrastaging (or systemic pelvic ± para-aortic lymphadenectomy if SLN mapping fails or if macroscopic nodal involvement is encountered). - **Fertility Preservation Note:** Conservative/fertility-sparing management (e.g., progestin therapy) is **contraindicated** because the tumor is FIGO Grade II (fertility preservation is restricted to well-differentiated FIGO Grade I endometrioid carcinoma strictly limited to the endometrium). 3. **Adjuvant Therapy Decision-Making (Post-Surgical Staging & Molecular Integration):** - Final adjuvant management will be determined by the integration of surgical-pathological stage and the completed molecular subgroup per ESGO-ESTRO-ESP guidelines: - **Low Risk** (e.g., Stage IA, FIGO Grade 2, LVSI-negative, NSMP/MMRd, or Stage I–II POLEmut): Observation alone; no adjuvant therapy required. - **Intermediate / High-Intermediate Risk** (e.g., Stage IB, FIGO Grade 2, NSMP/MMRd, or Stage IA with substantial LVSI): Vaginal brachytherapy (VBT) to optimize local pelvic control, or pelvic external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) if multiple adverse risk factors are present. - **High Risk** (e.g., any myometrial invasion in p53-abnormal tumors, or Stage III/nodal-positive disease): External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) combined with systemic chemotherapy (e.g., carboplatin and paclitaxel). 4. **Genetic Counseling & Screening:** - If MMR IHC reveals loss of mismatch repair proteins (MMRd), perform reflex *MLH1* promoter hypermethylation testing (if MLH1/PMS2 lost) and refer the patient for genetic counseling and germline testing for Lynch syndrome.
