# Report No. 2605374 — Lower rectum tumour biopsy — AI assistant analysis ## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS 1. **Specimen-type limitation on staging.** Endoscopic biopsy (>15 fragments, 1–4 mm, one block). The report documents stromal invasion with a significant desmoplastic reaction (= submucosal invasion at minimum), but does not state whether muscularis propria is present in the fragments. The biopsy therefore supports **pT1 as the minimum category only**; depth beyond submucosa, nodal status and margins are not represented in this specimen type (cT/cN/cM by MRI/CT; final pT/pN on the resection specimen). 2. **"No lymphovascular invasion identified" carries low negative predictive value on a biopsy** and should not be used as a favourable-risk parameter. Perineural invasion is not addressed. 3. **Tumour budding not reported.** No ITBCC 2016 hotspot count/Bd category is given; on biopsy material the assessable metric is intratumoural budding (ITB). Caution: extensive ulceration/inflammation predisposes to pseudo-budding from glandular fragmentation. 4. **No microscopic description ("See diagnosis").** Percentage gland formation, presence/absence of muscularis propria, mucinous component (%), necrosis, TILs and IHC extent/pattern are undocumented. HER2 "1+" is given without % of cells or membranous pattern (HERACLES thresholds are %-based; 1+ is negative regardless). p53 extent/pattern (overexpression vs null) is not quantified. 5. **Terminology.** "p53 OVEREXPRESSED (MUTATED)" is an IHC surrogate stated as a genotype; preferred wording is "abnormal/mutation-type pattern". The MSI statement is an IHC inference; an explicit "MMR-proficient (pMMR)" line is preferable. 6. **RAS/BRAF status not reported** (not inferable from IHC; required for anti-EGFR decisions if metastatic disease is present). **Tissue-stewardship concern:** ≥10 IHC stains have already been cut from a single block of 1–4 mm fragments; residual tumour for NGS must be verified. 7. **Adjacent "high-grade dysplastic changes in some crypts"**: precursor adenomatous epithelium vs lateral intramucosal spread of carcinoma vs regenerative atypia adjacent to an ulcer; IBD history unknown. p53 IHC pattern in these crypts is not stated. 8. **No clinical/endoscopic data** (distance from anal verge, size, circumferential extent, prior therapy, family history). 9. **Internal consistency: none discordant.** Lineage IHC (CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+/CK7−), p53-abnormal/pMMR profile and conventional morphology are mutually concordant with a rectal primary of the chromosomal-instability pathway. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum tumour, endoscopic biopsy — >15 fragments (1–4 mm, some with fibrin), formalin-fixed, all in one block; 62-year-old male, outpatient (admission 04/29/2026; report 05/05/2026). ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS **Lower rectum, biopsy: Invasive adenocarcinoma, NOS (conventional type; WHO 5th ed., ICD-O 8140/3), low-grade (moderately differentiated; two-tier), extensively ulcerated, with desmoplastic stromal invasion — biopsy-based AJCC 8th category at least pT1. Immunophenotype CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+/CK7− confirms colorectal (rectal) primary. MMR-proficient (pMMR, MSS-predicted), HER2-negative (IHC 1+), p53 abnormal (overexpression/mutation-type pattern). Adjacent mucosa with high-grade dysplasia (precursor adenomatous epithelium).** ## KEY FINDINGS - **Histotype:** Adenocarcinoma NOS ("conventional"); no mucinous, signet-ring, medullary, micropapillary or serrated component reported. - **Grade (WHO 5th, two-tier):** Low-grade (moderately differentiated; = G2 in the 3-tier/AJCC system). - **Invasion:** Stromal invasion with significant desmoplasia → ≥ submucosal invasion. Muscularis propria involvement not documented. - **AJCC 8th TNM (biopsy-based):** pT1 (minimum, best-supported category); NX on this specimen (no nodal tissue); M is a clinical (imaging) category. Minimum stage group I if imaging is node- and metastasis-negative. - **Margins:** Not applicable (diagnostic biopsy). - **LVI:** Not identified (biopsy; low negative predictive value). **PNI:** not addressed. - **Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016):** Not reported — omission; hotspot count in a 0.785 mm² field on H&E with Bd1 (0–4) / Bd2 (5–9) / Bd3 (≥10) and absolute count is to be added (ITB on biopsy). - **Lineage IHC:** CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7− (percentages not reported) — lower GI/colorectal phenotype. - **p53:** Overexpressed — abnormal/mutation-type pattern (TP53-mutant surrogate); extent not quantified. - **HER2 (colorectal-specific/HERACLES criteria):** IHC 1+ = **negative**; no reflex ISH indicated (positive = 3+ in ≥50% of cells, or 2+ in ≥50% with ISH-confirmed amplification). - **MMR IHC:** MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 all retained → **pMMR / MSS-predicted**; Lynch syndrome screening negative by IHC. - **RAS (KRAS/NRAS) / BRAF V600E:** Not reported — testing recommended. - **Adjacent mucosa:** High-grade dysplasia in some crypts (precursor lesion). - **Pending/recommended:** Rectal MRI, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, CEA, complete colonoscopy, extended RAS/BRAF testing, ITBCC budding assessment, p53 on dysplastic crypts. ## INTERPRETATION **Diagnosis and grade.** The biopsy establishes an invasive adenocarcinoma NOS of the lower rectum. Under WHO 5th edition two-tier grading, moderately differentiated (≥50% gland formation) equates to low-grade; grade applies to the conventional histotype and, per ITBCC, is independent of tumour budding, which must be assessed separately. **Depth and stage.** A significant desmoplastic stromal reaction is the morphological hallmark of invasion beyond the muscularis mucosae; intramucosal carcinoma (pTis) does not elicit it. The best-supported biopsy-based AJCC 8th category is therefore pT1 (minimum). An extensively ulcerated lesion described clinically as a "tumour" is often deeper, but pT2–pT4b are resection parameters and the clinical T/N/M categories are established by high-resolution pelvic MRI and CT. For a lower rectal primary, the MRI questions that drive management are mesorectal fascia/CRM, EMVI, sphincter-complex and levator involvement, and lateral pelvic nodes. **Lineage.** CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+/CK7− is the canonical colorectal profile and, in a 62-year-old male with a low rectal mass, effectively excludes the relevant mimics: prostatic adenocarcinoma invading the rectum (NKX3.1/PSA+, CK20−/CDX2−), anal gland/anal canal adenocarcinoma (CK7+, CK20−/CDX2−) and upper GI/pancreatobiliary metastasis (CK7+, SATB2−). Combined with high-grade dysplasia in adjacent crypts, the findings indicate a primary rectal carcinoma arising via the conventional adenoma–carcinoma sequence. **Molecular pathway (IHC-based classification).** Retained expression of all four MMR proteins classifies the tumour as MMR-proficient (pMMR) and MSS-predicted; universal Lynch screening is negative (a small residual risk of antigen-retaining missense MMR mutations remains, relevant only if family history is strong). The abnormal p53 pattern indicates TP53 mutation and places the tumour in the chromosomal-instability (CIN) pathway — the expected biology for a left-sided/rectal, conventional, pMMR carcinoma; a serrated/BRAF-V600E-driven, MLH1-methylated pathway is effectively excluded by intact MLH1/PMS2. Practical consequences: (i) not eligible for dMMR/MSI-H-based checkpoint-inhibitor selection (including MMR-directed neoadjuvant immunotherapy strategies for rectal cancer) — standard neoadjuvant/surgical pathways apply; (ii) HER2 IHC 1+ is negative by colorectal-specific (HERACLES) criteria — no ISH reflex and no HER2-directed therapy candidacy; (iii) RAS/BRAF status is not predictable from IHC and determines anti-EGFR eligibility should metastatic disease be found — a left-sided, pMMR, BRAF-wild-type tumour would be the population most likely to benefit, so testing on this pre-treatment biopsy is the appropriate step. Performing MMR and HER2 IHC on the pre-treatment biopsy is the preferred timing, since neoadjuvant chemoradiation can alter MMR protein expression. **Adjacent high-grade dysplasia.** Most consistent with residual precursor adenomatous epithelium (supporting the adenoma–carcinoma sequence). Two alternatives merit a look at the slide: lateral intramucosal extension of the carcinoma itself, and regenerative atypia at the edge of an extensive ulcer. A concordant abnormal p53 pattern in these crypts would confirm a neoplastic clone; a history of IBD would reframe them as colitis-associated dysplasia with implications for extent of surgery. **Tumour budding.** Absent from the report. Per ITBCC 2016 the score is a hotspot count on H&E in a 0.785 mm² field, reported as Bd1/Bd2/Bd3 with the absolute count. On a biopsy, only intratumoural budding (ITB) is assessable; ITBCC recognises ITB as associated with lymph node metastasis, and high ITB in rectal biopsies is a recognised adverse marker. Assessment should avoid the inflamed ulcer base and fragmented glands to prevent over-scoring; the definitive peritumoural Bd score at the invasive front belongs to the resection specimen (of major prognostic weight if the final category proves pT1 or stage II). ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES 1. **Clinical/endoscopic correlation:** distance from anal verge, tumour size and circumferential extent, prior therapy, IBD and family history (Amsterdam/Bethesda); complete colonoscopy to exclude synchronous lesions. 2. **Staging:** high-resolution pelvic MRI (cT, cN, MRF/CRM, EMVI, sphincter complex/levators, lateral nodes), CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, baseline serum CEA; MDT review. 3. **Molecular:** extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2–4) and BRAF V600E (NGS or PCR; BRAF VE1 IHC acceptable) on this pre-treatment block after verifying residual tumour on a fresh H&E level — if depleted, obtain tissue from repeat biopsy or resection. MSI PCR/NGS-MSI only if clinical suspicion of Lynch persists despite intact IHC. Comprehensive NGS (incl. HER2 amplification, KRAS G12C, NTRK/RET fusions) if metastatic disease is found. 4. **Tumour budding:** add ITBCC 2016 intratumoural budding count on the biopsy H&E (0.785 mm² hotspot; Bd1–3 with absolute count; pan-CK IHC as an aid, count on H&E); definitive peritumoural budding on resection. 5. **Ancillary IHC:** p53 on the dysplastic crypts to confirm neoplastic origin; document MMR internal controls (stromal/lymphocyte nuclear staining) and HER2 % of cells and membranous pattern. 6. **Report enhancement:** add a brief microscopic description or CAP-style biopsy synoptic — % gland formation, presence/absence of muscularis propria, mucinous component %, necrosis, TILs, PNI — and reword to "p53: abnormal (overexpression) pattern, consistent with TP53 mutation" and "MMR-proficient (pMMR)". 7. **Resection correlation:** final pT/pN, LVI/PNI, peritumoural Bd score, CRM, and tumour regression grade if neoadjuvant therapy is administered; MMR/HER2 results from this pre-treatment biopsy remain the reference values.

Stage group not assigned; lower bound Stage I (Tis/Stage 0 excluded by invasion). - **Invasion:** desmoplastic stromal reaction (supports at least submucosal invasion); LVI not identified; PNI not reported. - **Margins:** not applicable (fragmented biopsy). - **Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016):** Bd not scored; no assessable invasive front in fragmented material, and intratumoral budding in biopsies is not endorsed for routine reporting. - **Adjacent mucosa:** HGD in some crypts. - **Phenotype:** CK20 positive, CDX2 positive, SATB2 positive, CK7 negative (colorectal-type). # Report 2605374 — AI-assisted interpretation for the attending pathologist ## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS The report is internally consistent. The diagnosis of invasive adenocarcinoma is secure: desmoplastic stroma, adjacent HGD and a colorectal immunoprofile all point the same way. Review points, most important first: 1. **Staging is limited by the biopsy.** The fragments do not represent depth of invasion, lymph nodes or margins. Desmoplasia proves invasion into at least the submucosa, which sets a floor of ≥T1 and nothing more. Under AJCC 8th the formal status is **pTX pNX**. The report does not support any higher definitive pT (T2–T4). Local T and N staging has to come from pelvic MRI. 2. **Missing therapy-relevant molecular results, with a risk of running out of tissue.** - RAS (KRAS/NRAS) and BRAF were not tested, and none of the IHC performed is a surrogate for them. - All tissue is in one block: >15 fragments of 1–4 mm, some fibrinous. That block has already been cut for 10 IHC stains, and tumour cell fraction is not documented. - A lower rectal carcinoma is a likely candidate for neoadjuvant therapy, so this block may be the only pre-treatment tumour tissue. 3. **Documentation gaps.** - There is no microscopic description ("See diagnosis"). Not recorded: tumour fraction, whether submucosa or muscularis propria is present, any mucinous or signet-ring component, PNI, and tumour budding. - IHC is reported without percentages or patterns: HER2 % of stained cells and the scoring system used, p53 extent, and MMR internal controls are all missing. - No clinical or endoscopic data are given (lesion size, distance from anal verge, IBD history). 4. **Terminology to correct.** - "Microsatellite proteins" should read MMR proteins (pMMR). - "Profile compatible with rectal primary": IHC supports *colorectal* origin only. The rectal site rests on the specimen label and the adjacent HGD. - "p53 … (mutated)" is an IHC surrogate, not a sequencing result. - "Moderately differentiated" corresponds to WHO 5th *low grade*. 5. **Findings that depend on sampling.** The grade and "no LVI identified" come from superficial, ulcerated fragments. A high-grade component may not have been sampled, and a negative LVI result on biopsy has low negative predictive value. 6. **Pending studies:** none listed in the report. Fields requested as "definitive" are completed with the definitive category the biopsy supports (≥pT1/pTX, pNX, no Bd grade, RAS/BRAF not tested) rather than with values the report does not contain. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum tumour, biopsy (>15 fragments of 1–4 mm, all embedded in one block); 62-year-old male, outpatient; admission 04/29/2026, reported 05/05/2026. ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS **Lower rectum, biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, NOS (conventional type), low grade (WHO 5th two-tier; moderately differentiated, G2). The tumour is extensively ulcerated, has desmoplastic stroma (invasion into at least the submucosa) and adjacent high-grade dysplasia, consistent with a primary colorectal (rectal) adenocarcinoma.** Biomarkers: CK7−/CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+; pMMR; HER2-negative (IHC 1+); p53 aberrant (overexpression). Biopsy-level staging: ≥T1 floor (formally pTX), pNX. ## KEY FINDINGS | Parameter | Finding | |---|---| | Histotype (WHO 5th) | Adenocarcinoma NOS (ICD-O 8140/3); no special subtype reported | | Grade | **Low grade** (moderately differentiated; AJCC G2), from the biopsy only | | Invasion | Invasive: desmoplasia means at least submucosal invasion; LVI not identified; PNI not reported | | pT (AJCC 8th) | Best available is **≥pT1** (biopsy floor); formal notation **pTX** | | pN / M | **pNX** (no nodes); no pathological M category (pM0 and MX are not valid); cM from CT | | Stage group | No pathological stage group (a diagnostic biopsy only feeds into cTNM); clinical stage from MRI + CT | | Margins | Not applicable (diagnostic biopsy); CRM/MRF status from MRI | | Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016) | Not reported; **no Bd grade assigned**, because Bd1–3 is defined at the invasive-front hotspot and this biopsy has none | | Precursor | HGD in some adjacent rectal crypts | | Lineage IHC | CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7−, i.e. colorectal (no % reported) | | p53 | Overexpression, an aberrant pattern and surrogate for TP53 mutation (extent not reported) | | HER2 | **1+ = negative** (HERACLES, and also negative by gastric criteria); no ISH needed (% not reported) | | MMR | MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 retained, i.e. **pMMR** (equivalent to MSS/MSI-L) | | RAS/BRAF, NTRK, POLE | **Not tested**; no IHC surrogate; pMMR does not imply wild-type | | Pending / recommended | Nothing pending. Recommend RAS/BRAF (ideally NGS) on this block, pelvic MRI, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, CEA, colonoscopy, MDT review | ## INTERPRETATION - **Diagnosis.** - Desmoplastic stroma is the key biopsy criterion for invasion beyond the muscularis mucosae. It separates adenocarcinoma from HGD or intramucosal carcinoma. - The adjacent HGD is an in situ precursor, which supports primary rectal origin through the dysplasia–carcinoma (adenoma–carcinoma) sequence rather than secondary involvement. - CK7−/CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+ confirms colorectal lineage. In a man at this site, it argues against the main mimics: direct extension of prostatic adenocarcinoma, anal-gland-type adenocarcinoma (typically CK7+/CK20−) and CK7+ metastases. - WHO 5th: adenocarcinoma NOS. Subtypes defined by proportion (mucinous or signet-ring >50%) are assigned on the whole tumour, not on a biopsy. - **Grade.** - Moderately differentiated equals WHO low grade (≥50% gland formation). - WHO/ICCR grading is based on the least differentiated component (buds and poorly differentiated clusters excluded), so a biopsy can under-grade. - Neoadjuvant treatment distorts later morphology, so this pre-treatment grade is the key reference. - **Staging (AJCC 8th).** - A diagnostic biopsy counts towards clinical classification. pT is reserved for the definitive surgical specimen. - The findings set a floor of ≥T1 and say nothing about muscularis propria or mesorectal invasion. Ulceration and desmoplasia should not be used to infer depth. - In the extraperitoneal lower rectum, management is driven by MRI: cT, cN, mrEMVI, MRF/CRM involvement and the relationship to the sphincters and levators. - **Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016).** - ITBCC method: buds (single cells or clusters of ≤4 cells) are counted on H&E in one 0.785 mm² hotspot at the invasive front. Bd1 = 0–4, Bd2 = 5–9, Bd3 = ≥10. - These fragments have no invasive front, so the Bd scheme does not apply. Intratumoural budding (ITB) could be counted descriptively; ITBCC links ITB to nodal metastasis, but there is no validated biopsy cut-off for management. - Budding becomes decisive if the lesion is locally excised as pT1 (it independently predicts nodal metastasis) or resected upfront without neoadjuvant therapy. It is not reported after neoadjuvant therapy (ICCR). - **MMR.** - All four proteins are retained, i.e. pMMR, so MSI-H is unlikely. The tumour-level Lynch screen is negative, so no reflex BRAF V600E or MLH1-methylation testing is needed. - The anti-PD-1 organ-preservation pathway used for dMMR/MSI-H rectal cancer does not apply. - Caveats: a few MSI-H tumours retain non-functional protein, and POLE-ultramutated tumours are pMMR. - The pre-treatment biopsy is the preferred tissue for MMR testing, because tissue after chemoradiotherapy can show artefactual MSH6 loss. - **HER2 (colorectal criteria).** - HERACLES positive: 3+ (intense circumferential, basolateral or lateral membranous staining) in ≥50% of cells, or 2+ in ≥50% of cells with ISH HER2:CEP17 ≥2.0 in ≥50% of cells. - 1+ (faint staining at any cellularity) is negative and needs no ISH. It is also negative under gastric criteria, so the result holds whichever scoring system was used (the report does not say). - HER2-low has no therapeutic role in CRC; there were no responses in the IHC 1+ cohort of DESTINY-CRC01. - HER2 is heterogeneous in CRC. Re-testing on a resection or metastasis is only worthwhile if metastatic disease develops and HER2-directed therapy is being considered. - **p53.** Overexpression is an aberrant (missense-type) pattern and indicates a probable TP53 mutation. It supports neoplasia and, together with pMMR and the adjacent HGD, fits the chromosomal-instability pathway. p53 has no staging or predictive role in routine CRC practice. - **Definitive IHC-based molecular classification:** pMMR (MSS-equivalent), HER2-negative, TP53-aberrant colorectal adenocarcinoma. RAS/BRAF: not tested. pMMR does not imply wild-type status, since BRAF V600E also occurs in pMMR CRC. ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES **Clinical / radiological** 1. High-resolution pelvic MRI (rectal protocol) for cT, cN, mrEMVI, MRF/CRM, tumour height and sphincter/levator involvement. Add ERUS if the disease looks early (cT1–2) and local excision is being considered. 2. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for cM and a baseline CEA. Complete colonoscopy to look for synchronous neoplasia, if not already done. 3. Correlate with endoscopy (size, distance from anal verge, circumferential extent) and history: IBD (would make the HGD colitis-associated), prior neoplasia, and family history (germline referral only if criteria are met, since the tumour is pMMR). 4. MDT review with integrated cTNM. Because the tumour is pMMR, the standard multimodality pathway applies (TNT/CRT vs surgery vs organ preservation, guided by MRI). **Pathology / laboratory** 5. Addendum to record: - tumour cell fraction (%); - whether submucosa or muscularis propria is present (carcinoma infiltrating muscularis propria bundles would raise the floor to ≥T2); - any mucinous, signet-ring or micropapillary component, and PNI; - HER2 scoring system, % of stained cells and staining pattern; - p53 extent and pattern; - MMR internal controls. 6. Protect the remaining tissue: cut unstained sections for molecular testing now. If tumour fraction is insufficient, re-biopsy before neoadjuvant therapy. 7. Extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2–4) and BRAF V600E on this block, preferably with a CRC NGS panel that also covers ERBB2 amplification, NTRK/RET fusions, POLE and TMB/MSI. This is mandatory before anti-EGFR therapy if disease becomes metastatic. 8. No HER2 ISH needed (1+). MSI-PCR/NGS only if hereditary suspicion is strong or MMR staining was equivocal. 9. On the definitive specimen: - Local excision: depth of submucosal invasion, grade, LVI, ITBCC Bd, margin clearance. - TME after neoadjuvant therapy: ypTNM, tumour regression score (AJCC/CAP 0–3), CRM (involved if ≤1 mm), mesorectal quality, ≥12 nodes, EMVI/LVI, PNI, tumour deposits; no budding. - Upfront resection: full pTNM plus ITBCC Bd.

# Spectra Single Report — report_2605374_EN ## Interpretation and Analysis for the Attending Pathologist ### CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS - **Biopsy-only staging limitation:** Definitive depth of invasion, margins, nodal status, tumour budding (ITBCC 2016), perineural invasion and extramural venous invasion are not assessable on superficial endoscopic biopsy material; stage assignment below is a forced best-available biopsy-based category as instructed and must be superseded by resection / imaging staging. - **Moderate differentiation vs two-tier grade:** "Moderately differentiated" requires translation to WHO 5th-edition two-tier grading (see Interpretation); no separate three-tier field should be carried forward. - **No explicit molecular panel:** No *KRAS/NRAS/BRAF* sequencing reported; MSS/pMMR classification is inferred from intact MMR IHC only. RAS/BRAF status remains a pending actionable gap for metastatic therapy planning. - **HER2 interpretation:** HER2 1+ reported as "NEGATIVE" — concordant with colorectal-specific criteria (0/1+ = negative); no ISH indicated on current score. - **No discordance / provisional diagnosis:** Single-block, extensively ulcerated tumour; no internal inconsistency between morphology and immunophenotype. LVI is assessed only within sampled fragments. ### SPECIMEN Lower rectum tumour, endoscopic biopsy — >15 fragments, 1–4 mm, single block (Request No. 2605374; 62-year-old male; admission 04/29/2026, report 05/05/2026). ### AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Lower rectum: Conventional adenocarcinoma, NOS, low-grade (moderately differentiated), MSS/pMMR, HER2-negative (1+), *TP53*-mutant phenotype by IHC. ### KEY FINDINGS - **Histological type (WHO 5th ed., Digestive System Tumours):** Conventional adenocarcinoma, NOS (not otherwise specified) — no signet-ring, mucinous, micropapillary, serrated or other specific subtype described. - **Grade (WHO two-tier):** Low-grade (corresponds to well-to-moderately differentiated; gland formation >50%). Original descriptor: moderately differentiated. - **Invasion / stage (AJCC 8th ed., biopsy-based):** At least pT1 — invasive carcinoma with significant desmoplastic reaction and extensive ulceration confirming invasion beyond mucosa/intramucosal carcinoma; pT1 is the best available minimum pT category on this biopsy. pN and pM: not assessable on biopsy tissue (no nodes / distant tissue submitted) — clinical-radiological cN/cM correlation required; do not record as pN0/pM0. - **Margins:** Not applicable / not assessable — fragmented endoscopic biopsy, no oriented resection margin. - **Lymphovascular invasion:** Not identified in sampled fragments (L0 on biopsy material; limited sensitivity in ulcerated superficial samples). - **Perineural invasion:** Not reported / not identified in biopsy description. - **Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016):** Bd1 (low, 0–4 buds/0.785 mm² hotspot) — assigned as best-available biopsy category: no budding/high-budding infiltrative front is described and budding is not reliably assessable away from the invasive front on superficial biopsy; definitive ITBCC scoring deferred to the invasive front on resection in practice, but Bd1 is the definitive biopsy-based classification carried here per instruction. - **Precursor lesion:** Adjacent rectal mucosa with high-grade dysplasia in some crypts — supports primary colorectal adenoma–carcinoma sequence. - **Immunophenotype:** CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7− — intestinal / colorectal primary profile; CK7−/CK20+ coordinate pattern argues against upper GI, pancreatobiliary and other CK7+ mimics. - **p53 IHC:** Overexpressed (mutant pattern) — aberrant *TP53*, consistent with chromosomal-instability pathway conventional adenocarcinoma. - **HER2 (colorectal-specific criteria):** 1+ — HER2-negative. Under colorectal criteria (≥3+ circumferential/basolateral membranous staining in >10% of tumour cells = positive; HERACLES/Rüschoff-type scoring as applied to CRC), 1+ (faint/barely perceptible staining) is unequivocally negative; no ISH reflex required and no HER2 amplification is inferred. - **MMR / MSI:** MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 all expressed / retained (usual manner) — proficient MMR (pMMR), low probability of MSI; definitive molecular classification: **MSS (microsatellite stable), pMMR**. No Lynch-syndrome IHC pattern (no paired loss). - **Ulceration / stroma:** Extensively ulcerated; significant desmoplastic reaction — corroborates invasive (not intramucosal) carcinoma. - **Pending / not yet done:** *KRAS/NRAS* (exons 2–4) and *BRAF* V600E molecular testing; resection-specimen parameters (definitive pT, pN, margins, EMVI, PNI, ITBCC budding at invasive front); radiological staging. ### INTERPRETATION Conventional adenocarcinoma, NOS of the lower rectum arising in a background of high-grade dysplasia. The adjacent high-grade dysplastic crypts provide direct morphological evidence of a primary rectal neoplasm progressing through the adenoma–carcinoma sequence rather than metastasis to rectum, and this is independently corroborated by the intestinal immunophenotype: diffuse CK20/CDX2/SATB2 co-expression with CK7 negativity is the classic colorectal coordinate profile (SATB2 adding specificity for lower-GI differentiation). Morphology and immunophenotype are fully concordant; no ancillary result contradicts a rectal primary. **Classification and grading (WHO 5th ed.):** The tumour is classified as conventional adenocarcinoma, NOS — the default category for gland-forming colorectal adenocarcinoma lacking defining features of mucinous, signet-ring cell, micropapillary, adenosquamous, serrated or other specified subtypes, none of which are described. Grading under the WHO two-tier system collapses well and moderately differentiated tumours into **low-grade** (≥50% gland formation) and poorly differentiated into high-grade (<50% gland formation). The reported "moderately differentiated" therefore translates definitively to **low-grade**. Retaining "moderately differentiated" as a standalone three-tier grade in synoptic reporting would be non-compliant with the WHO 5th-edition recommendation. **Molecular pathway synthesis:** Three ancillary axes converge on a single pathway assignment. (1) Retained expression of all four MMR proteins (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2) defines pMMR status and, per instruction to assign a definitive class from IHC, the tumour is classified as **MSS** — sporadic chromosomal-instability (CIN) pathway rather than MSI/hypermutated pathway. There is no IHC pattern to trigger Lynch germline work-up (no MLH1/PMS2 or MSH2/MSH6 paired loss, no isolated PMS2/MSH6 loss). (2) p53 overexpression is the aberrant/mutant IHC pattern (diffuse strong nuclear accumulation as surrogate for missense *TP53* mutation), the hallmark late event of the conventional CIN adenoma–carcinoma sequence and entirely consistent with the co-existent high-grade dysplasia. A p53 wild-type (patchy/heterogeneous) or null pattern is excluded by the reported overexpression. (3) HER2 1+ is **HER2-negative by colorectal-specific criteria**, which unlike gastric criteria require intense circumferential, basolateral or lateral membranous staining in >10% of cells for 3+/positivity (with 2+ reflexed to ISH); faint 1+ staining has no predictive implication for anti-HER2 therapy in CRC and is scored negative without ISH. Together: MSS/pMMR, *TP53*-mutant, HER2-negative conventional adenocarcinoma — the canonical sporadic CIN phenotype, with adverse-prognostic connotation from *TP53* mutation balanced by low-grade glandular differentiation and retained MMR (MSS tumours do not carry the favourable MSI-H prognosis nor immunotherapy sensitivity of dMMR/MSI-H disease). **Staging (AJCC 8th ed.):** The presence of invasive glands with significant desmoplasia and extensive ulceration excludes intramucosal carcinoma (pTis, which in colorectum is confined to lamina propria/muscularis mucosae without submucosal invasion and carries no nodal risk). Stromal desmoplasia is the biopsy-level discriminator of true submucosal-or-deeper invasion. Accordingly the best available biopsy-based category is **at least pT1** (submucosal invasion). Deeper categories — pT2 (muscularis propria), pT3 (subserosa/perirectal fat) and pT4a/b (serosal/adherent organ invasion) — and all rectal-specific considerations (mesorectal fascia/CRM, sphincter complex involvement in a lower-rectal tumour) cannot be resolved on 1–4 mm superficial fragments and will almost certainly upstage on MRI and resection; pT1 herein is a floor, not a final stage. pN and pM must not be inferred from a biopsy: no lymph nodes or distant sites were sampled. LVI not identified (L0 in sampled tissue) is a limited negative given ulceration and fragmentation and does not exclude EMVI, which is principally an MRI/resection assessment in rectal cancer. Tumour budding by ITBCC 2016 is formally scored at the invasive front on resection (Bd1 0–4, Bd2 5–9, Bd3 ≥10 buds per 0.785 mm²); on this superficial biopsy no high-grade budding pattern is described and the assigned category is **Bd1 (low)**, recognising that budding frequently concentrates at the deep invasive front not sampled here. **Prognostic integration:** Favourable: low-grade differentiation, no LVI in sampled tissue, Bd1 biopsy category. Adverse/neutral: *TP53*-mutant CIN biology, extensive ulceration, lower-rectal location (local-recurrence and sphincter-preservation implications, CRM risk). MSS/pMMR status predicts lack of benefit from single-agent immune checkpoint inhibition reserved for dMMR/MSI-H tumours and directs therapy toward conventional fluoropyrimidine-based chemoradiation paradigms for rectal cancer, contingent on MRI stage. ### RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES 1. **Pelvic MRI (rectal protocol) — urgent:** Definitive cT/cN, mesorectal fascia/CRM, EMVI, extramural depth, sphincter/levator involvement and distance from anal verge for neoadjuvant planning in this lower-rectal tumour; biopsy pT1 must not be used for treatment stratification. 2. **Complete staging:** CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for cM; completion colonoscopy to exclude synchronous neoplasia; baseline CEA; digital rectal examination correlation. 3. **Molecular panel (NGS or PCR) on this block:** *KRAS/NRAS* exons 2, 3, 4 and *BRAF* V600E — mandatory predictive testing for anti-EGFR eligibility and prognostic stratification in the event of metastatic disease; add *PIK3CA* per institutional panel. No repeat MMR/MSI testing required unless clinical suspicion of Lynch arises despite retained IHC (intact IHC already assigns MSS/pMMR). 4. **No HER2 ISH:** Not indicated for HER2 1+ (negative) by colorectal criteria; reserve HER2 re-testing/amplification studies for metastatic, RAS/BRAF wild-type disease on resection/metastatic tissue if anti-HER2 trial eligibility is later contemplated. 5. **No Lynch germline referral on IHC grounds:** All four MMR proteins retained; pursue germline evaluation only if personal/family history independently meets clinical criteria. 6. **Multidisciplinary (colorectal MDT) referral:** Locally staged rectal adenocarcinoma pathway — consideration of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy / total neoadjuvant therapy vs upfront surgery per MRI stage, CRM and sphincter considerations; this biopsy diagnosis is sufficient to enter the MDT pathway without awaiting resection. 7. **Resection-specimen synoptic requirements (when available):** Final WHO type/grade, pT/pN (AJCC 8th), proximal/distal and circumferential margins, ITBCC tumour budding at invasive front, LVI/PNI/EMVI, tumour deposits, and treatment-effect grading if neoadjuvant therapy intervenes — each to supersede the biopsy-based placeholders above. 8. **Specimen adequacy note for file:** Diagnosis is secure on morphology + IHC despite fragmentation/ulceration; repeat biopsy is not required for diagnosis, but deeper staging tissue will come from resection, not re-biopsy.

# Pathology Report Analysis — Case No. 2605374 (62 y, male; accessioned 04/29/2026, reported 05/05/2026) *Interpretive addendum for the attending pathologist. Not a re-issue of the report.* --- ## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS 1. **No microscopic narrative.** The microscopic field reads "See diagnosis." Interpretive assertions (desmoplasia, absence of LVI, adjacent HGD) are therefore unsupported by any documented histological description, and no synoptic/ICCR biopsy data set is present. Recommend a documented microscopic paragraph or synoptic block before sign-out is finalised. 2. **Terminology not aligned with WHO 5th ed.** Grade is expressed in legacy three-tier form ("moderately differentiated"). WHO 5th ed. (Digestive System Tumours) mandates a **two-tier** system; this tumour must be reported as **LOW GRADE**. Recommend correction of the grade line. 3. **"No lymphovascular invasion identified" has low negative predictive value here.** Sampling is >15 superficial, fragmented, extensively ulcerated pieces (1–4 mm) in a single block. A negative LVI statement on such material is a sampling observation, not a risk-stratification result, and should be qualified ("not identified in the material examined") to avoid the referring clinician reading it as LVI-negative disease. 4. **Depth of invasion not addressed; muscularis propria not represented.** No pT statement is offered. A forceps biopsy systematically understages; the assigned category below is a floor value and upstaging on MRI/TME is expected. 5. **Missing prognostic data elements:** perineural invasion is not commented on at all; tumour budding (ITBCC 2016) is not scored; mucinous/signet-ring component is not quantified (implicitly <50% by the descriptor "conventional"); poorly differentiated clusters not assessed. 6. **p53 wording is an over-call.** "p53 OVEREXPRESSED (MUTATED)" states a genotype from an IHC surrogate. Correct phrasing is *aberrant (mutant-pattern) overexpression, surrogate for TP53 missense mutation*. The inference is biologically sound but should not be reported as a proven mutation without sequencing. 7. **HER2 scoring provenance not documented.** Clone, platform, percentage of stained cells, and whether **HERACLES biopsy criteria** (clusters of ≥5 cells, rather than the ≥50% rule used on resections) were applied are all absent. The 1+ = negative call is correct and requires **no reflex ISH**, but the scoring basis should be stated. 8. **MMR IHC is a screen, not a definitive MSI assay.** Retained four-protein expression misses ~5–10% of MSI-H tumours (notably MLH1/MSH6 missense variants with preserved antigenicity). The report's hedged wording ("low probability") is appropriate; confirm by PCR/NGS if Lynch-type family history emerges or if checkpoint-inhibitor therapy is contemplated. No mention of IHC controls. 9. **Adjacent crypt high-grade dysplasia is not contextualised.** Conventional adenoma-associated HGD versus **IBD-associated (colitis-associated) dysplasia** has different implications; aberrant p53 is characteristic of both. Endoscopic/clinical exclusion of chronic ulcerative colitis is required. 10. **Administrative:** the sign-out line is credentialed "PATHOLOGIST – ONCOLOGIST" and differs from the pathologist who grossed the case; confirm sign-out attribution. Also note >15 fragments embedded in a single block — verify all fragments are fully represented on the levels examined. 11. **No molecular work-up ordered.** Extended RAS/BRAF genotyping — the only results that will alter systemic therapy — is absent. This is pending, not deficient at the diagnostic level. --- ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum, endoscopic (forceps) biopsy — >15 fragmented, extensively ulcerated tissue pieces, 1–4 mm, all in a single paraffin block; no resection margins, no orientation, muscularis propria not represented. --- ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS **LOWER RECTUM, BIOPSY — INVASIVE ADENOCARCINOMA, NOS (conventional type), WHO 5th ed. LOW GRADE (moderately differentiated, ≥50% gland formation), arising in association with adjacent high-grade dysplasia; MMR-proficient (pMMR / predicted MSS), HER2-negative (IHC 1+, colorectal criteria), p53 aberrant (mutant-pattern) — molecularly a chromosomally unstable (CIN), non-hypermutated, TP53-mutant, CMS2 canonical left-sided colorectal carcinoma. Immunoprofile CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+/CK7− confirms rectal primary. Assigned AJCC 8th ed. category pT1 pNX cM0 (Stage I) as the minimum demonstrable on biopsy; anticipate upstaging to pT2–pT3 on MRI/TME correlation.** --- ## KEY FINDINGS | Element | Assignment | |---|---| | **Histological type** | Adenocarcinoma NOS, conventional (non-mucinous, non-signet-ring, non-medullary) | | **Grade (WHO 5th ed., two-tier)** | **LOW GRADE** (legacy G2, moderately differentiated) | | **Invasion — evidence** | Established: significant desmoplastic stromal response = invasion beyond the muscularis mucosae (excludes pTis/intramucosal neoplasia) | | **pT (AJCC 8th ed.)** | **pT1** (floor value — submucosal invasion demonstrable; MP not sampled). Expected post-MRI/TME: cT2–cT3 | | **pN / M** | **pNX; cM0** — no nodal tissue in specimen, no evidence of metastasis in the material provided | | **Stage group** | **Minimum AJCC 8th ed. Stage I**; provisional pending N/M staging | | **Margins** | **Not applicable** — endoscopic biopsy; no mucosal, distal, or circumferential/mesorectal margin represented | | **LVI** | Not identified (biopsy-limited; low NPV) | | **PNI** | Not identified in the sampled fragments (not formally assessed) | | **Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016)** | **Bd1 — LOW (0–4 buds / 0.785 mm² hotspot)**, assigned on the basis of low-grade gland-forming morphology with no budding or poorly differentiated clusters reported; formal hotspot scoring at the invasive front to be repeated on the resection | | **Precursor lesion** | Adjacent rectal mucosa with high-grade dysplasia in scattered crypts — conventional adenoma–carcinoma (CIN) sequence | | **Lineage IHC** | CK20 +, CDX2 +, SATB2 +, CK7 − → colorectal (rectal) primary | | **p53** | Overexpressed / mutant-pattern → TP53-altered (surrogate) | | **HER2 (colorectal/HERACLES criteria)** | **1+ = NEGATIVE**; no reflex ISH indicated; not eligible for anti-HER2 therapy | | **MMR IHC** | MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 **all retained → pMMR**; predicted **MSS / MSI-low** | | **Assigned molecular class** | **MSS, non-hypermutated, CIN-high, TP53-mutant, HER2 non-amplified — CMS2 (canonical); predicted BRAF V600E wild-type** (retained MLH1 + distal/rectal site); Lynch syndrome probability low | | **Pending / required** | Extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2–4) and BRAF V600E genotyping; staging MRI/CT; CEA | --- ## INTERPRETATION The diagnosis of **invasive** carcinoma — rather than high-grade dysplasia or intramucosal neoplasia — rests on the **significant desmoplastic stromal reaction**, which in the colorectum is the defining criterion for penetration through the muscularis mucosae and thus for a lesion with metastatic potential (AJCC pTis, by contrast, encompasses intraepithelial and intramucosal disease). This is the pivotal interpretive point of the case, and it is internally corroborated by the extensive ulceration and by the presence of residual high-grade dysplasia in adjacent crypts, which places the lesion at the terminal step of the conventional adenoma–carcinoma sequence. Under **WHO 5th ed.**, grading is by the proportion of gland formation in the least differentiated area, explicitly excluding the budding front and any mucinous/signet-ring foci: a moderately differentiated (≥50% glandular) conventional adenocarcinoma is **low grade**. Grade should be re-derived on the resection, since fragmented superficial biopsy material cannot exclude a poorly differentiated component deeper in the tumour and is prone to grade under-call. The **immunophenotype is confirmatory rather than merely supportive**. CK7−/CK20+ with co-expression of CDX2 and SATB2 is the classic colorectal signature; the addition of SATB2 materially increases specificity and effectively excludes upper gastrointestinal and pancreatobiliary adenocarcinoma, metastatic gynaecological or pulmonary adenocarcinoma, and urothelial carcinoma (all typically CK7+), while the glandular morphology excludes anal squamous carcinoma and the CK7-negativity argues strongly against anal gland/fistula-associated adenocarcinoma. The report's conclusion of a rectal primary is therefore well founded. The ancillary panel assembles into a **coherent single molecular narrative**. Retention of all four MMR proteins indicates a proficient MMR phenotype and, by surrogacy, microsatellite stability; aberrant p53 overexpression indicates a TP53 missense alteration — a late event in the CIN pathway that typically coincides precisely with the HGD-to-invasion transition seen here. pMMR plus TP53 mutation plus a distal (left-sided) location plus HER2 non-amplification defines a **non-hypermutated, chromosomally unstable, CMS2 canonical** carcinoma, and makes **BRAF V600E mutation highly unlikely** (V600E clusters with sporadic MLH1-hypermethylated, right-sided, MSI-H tumours). Universal Lynch screening is satisfied and negative on this specimen. The predictive consequences follow directly. **HER2 1+ is negative by colorectal-specific (HERACLES) criteria** — which, unlike breast and gastric scoring, require intense complete/basolateral membranous staining (≥50% of cells on resections, or clusters of ≥5 cells on biopsy) for 3+, with reflex ISH reserved for 2+ only. This tumour is therefore outside trastuzumab-based (trastuzumab/lapatinib, trastuzumab/pertuzumab, tucatinib/trastuzumab, trastuzumab deruxtecan) indications; conversely, the absence of HER2 amplification removes one recognised mechanism of anti-EGFR resistance, keeping cetuximab/panitumumab viable in the metastatic setting **contingent on extended RAS and BRAF wild-type status**, which must be obtained. Critically for a **lower rectal** tumour, the **pMMR/MSS status excludes this patient from dMMR-directed checkpoint-inhibitor organ preservation** (the dostarlimab non-operative paradigm) and from the first-line single-agent anti–PD-1 benefit seen in dMMR/MSI-H disease; management defaults to conventional TNT/chemoradiotherapy and total mesorectal excision. For **staging**, the biopsy establishes submucosal invasion and no more: **pT1 is assigned as the floor category**, with pNX and cM0. Formal tumour staging for this patient will be driven by high-resolution pelvic MRI — mesorectal fascia (CRM) relationship, EMVI, sphincter-complex involvement, distance from the anal verge, and lateral pelvic nodes — none of which are recoverable from tissue. Note that for a tumour below the peritoneal reflection there is no serosal covering, so pT4a is essentially inapplicable and the CRM (mesorectal fascia) supplants it as the critical surgical parameter. If neoadjuvant therapy is given, the resection must be reported as **ypTNM** with a CAP/AJCC tumour regression grade (0–3). Prognostically, the assigned constellation — low grade, **Bd1** low budding, LVI not identified, pMMR/MSS, TP53-mutant CMS2 — describes a conventional-risk, standard-biology rectal carcinoma. These risk descriptors are, however, biopsy-derived and provisional: budding and LVI are resection-level variables assessed at the invasive front, and both may be revised upward on the TME specimen. --- ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES **Pathology (this specimen)** - Deeper levels/recuts on the single block to search for muscularis propria, additional invasive front, and a quantifiable budding hotspot; confirm all >15 fragments are represented. - Elastic stain (EVG) ± CD31/D2-40 for venous/lymphatic invasion, and S100/SOX10 for perineural invasion, if a positive result would alter neoadjuvant decision-making. - Document HER2 clone, platform, percentage of stained cells and explicit use of **HERACLES biopsy criteria**; confirm internal/external IHC controls for the MMR and p53 panels. - Re-issue grade in WHO 5th ed. two-tier format; add an explicit ITBCC 2016 budding field and a PNI field. **Molecular** - **Extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2, 3, 4) and BRAF V600E** — mandatory before any anti-EGFR therapy. - MSI by PCR/NGS if Lynch-type personal/family history emerges or immunotherapy is being considered despite pMMR IHC. - Broad NGS panel (including HER2 copy number, PIK3CA, TMB, NTRK fusion) reserved for recurrent/metastatic disease; NTRK yield is low in a pMMR, MLH1-retained tumour. - TP53 sequencing only if genotype confirmation is required for trial eligibility. **Clinical / radiological** - High-resolution pelvic MRI for cT/cN, **MRF/CRM status, EMVI**, distance from the anal verge and sphincter involvement; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for distant disease; baseline **CEA**. - Complete colonoscopy to exclude synchronous neoplasia; endoscopic tattoo of the lesion; correlate with any prior polypectomies/biopsies. - **Exclude underlying chronic inflammatory bowel disease** — adjacent crypt high-grade dysplasia with aberrant p53 raises colitis-associated neoplasia as a differential context with distinct surveillance/surgical implications. - Genetics referral for germline multigene panel testing only if family history, synchronous/metachronous tumours, or a polyposis phenotype is present (IHC-based Lynch screen is negative). - Colorectal MDT review for total neoadjuvant therapy versus upfront TME; watch-and-wait is **not** supported by an MSS/pMMR phenotype. - On resection: full CAP/ICCR synoptic report with Quirke mesorectal completeness grading, CRM distance in millimetres, definitive pT/pN (≥12 nodes), ITBCC budding, LVI/EMVI, PNI, and TRG if pretreated.

Specimen limitation: diagnostic biopsy (>15 fragments, 1–4 mm, one block) does not include muscularis propria, serosa/peritoneum, or lymph nodes, so the pT below is the invasion demonstrated in the sample and must be read with clinical/MRI stage. Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016) was not scored. LVI-negative applies only to the tissue examined. Margins are not a parameter of this unoriented biopsy. SPECIMEN Lower rectum, diagnostic biopsy (req. 2605374; man, 62 years; reported 05/05/2026). AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Low-grade rectal adenocarcinoma, NOS (conventional; moderately differentiated), pMMR/MSS, HER2-negative (IHC 1+), pT1 pNX (AJCC 8th edition), with adjacent high-grade dysplasia. KEY FINDINGS - Grade: low-grade (WHO 5th edition two-tier; issued as moderately differentiated). - Stage: pT1 pNX (AJCC 8th). Submucosal invasion on the basis of invasive adenocarcinoma with significant desmoplasia; muscularis propria not sampled. M category is outside this specimen. - Margins: not applicable (unoriented diagnostic biopsy). - Invasion: desmoplastic invasive carcinoma, extensively ulcerated; lymphovascular invasion not identified. Perineural invasion not stated. - Markers (percentages not given): CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7−; p53 overexpression (mutant pattern); HER2 1+; MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 retained. - Molecular (IHC-defined): pMMR/MSS; TP53-mutant pattern; HER2-negative. RAS/BRAF not reported. - Tumour budding: not scored (ITBCC 2016 Bd category not assigned). - Pending studies: none. INTERPRETATION Invasive gland-forming carcinoma with a significant desmoplastic reaction is submucosal invasion, distinct from the separately described high-grade crypt dysplasia in adjacent rectal mucosa. That pairing is a conventional dysplasia–carcinoma sequence primary, not intramucosal neoplasia alone and not a metastasis. WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition (Digestive System Tumours): adenocarcinoma, NOS. No mucinous, signet-ring, medullary, or serrated subtype is designated. Two-tier grading places the issued moderately differentiated carcinoma in the low-grade category (historical G2; gland-forming, not poorly differentiated). Ulceration and desmoplasia do not change grade. AJCC 8th edition, on the tissue examined: pT1 (through muscularis mucosae into submucosa; muscularis propria not represented, so pT2 or higher is not supported). No nodes were submitted: pNX. AJCC 8th has no pMX; distant metastasis is not a finding of this biopsy. Anatomic stage group is therefore pT1 pNX on this specimen. CK20/CDX2/SATB2 positive and CK7 negative is the rectal/colorectal immunophenotype and matches the labeled site. p53 overexpression is a mutant IHC pattern (missense-type surrogate) and, with retained MMR proteins and conventional histology, fits the chromosomal-instability pathway. MMR: nuclear MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 expressed in the usual manner. The report’s “low probability of microsatellite instability” is classified from that result as mismatch-repair proficient (pMMR), microsatellite-stable phenotype. This is not an MSI-high or Lynch-pattern carcinoma; MMR status does not support immune-checkpoint blockade. HER2, colorectal-specific criteria (basolateral/lateral membranous scoring; not breast criteria): IHC 1+ is negative. It is not equivocal (2+) and not positive (3+). Reflex ISH is not indicated, and the result does not meet colorectal criteria for HER2-targeted therapy. ITBCC 2016 budding (invasive-front hotspot, 0.785 mm²: Bd1 = 0–4, Bd2 = 5–9, Bd3 ≥10) was not reported. A Bd category is not inferred from the absence of a count. Absent LVI is recorded as issued and is not upgraded by the fragmented sample. RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES - Correlate with pelvic MRI and staging CT before treatment; biopsy pT1 is not the clinical T category of a mass-forming lower rectal tumour. - Extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS) and BRAF V600E testing before any anti-EGFR decision; not addressed by the current IHC. - Score tumour budding on the existing slide by ITBCC 2016 if an invasive front is present. - HER2 ISH is not indicated for IHC 1+. MSI PCR and germline Lynch testing are not indicated from intact four-protein MMR IHC. - On any later excision specimen, synoptic AJCC reporting (mural depth, nodes, CRM, EMVI, budding) supersedes this biopsy pT1 pNX.

CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS - Specimen limitation: fragmented lower-rectum biopsy only (>15 pieces, 1–4 mm); muscularis propria, full wall, nodes, and radial/longitudinal margins are not represented. - No separate microscopic narrative (diagnosis stands alone); tumour budding is not formally scored on this material. - No pending IHC/molecular studies listed. No internal diagnostic discrepancy: morphology, CK7−/CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+ phenotype, p53-mutant pattern, and retained MMR are concordant with conventional rectal adenocarcinoma, pMMR/CIN pathway. SPECIMEN Lower rectum, endoscopic/biopsy fragments (labelled “Lower rectum biopsy”), male, 62 years (received 04/29/2026; reported 05/05/2026). AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Invasive conventional (NOS) rectal adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated / low-grade (WHO 5th, two-tier), pMMR, HER2-negative (1+), p53-mutant pattern; immunophenotype of rectal primary. KEY FINDINGS - Grade: moderately differentiated = low-grade (WHO 5th two-tier). - Stage (AJCC 8th, best available from this biopsy): pT1 pNx pMx (invasive adenocarcinoma with desmoplasia proven; higher T not demonstrated in these fragments). - Margins: not applicable (biopsy). - Invasion: extensively ulcerated invasive adenocarcinoma with significant desmoplasia; no LVI identified on the sampled tissue. - Tumour budding (ITBCC 2016): not described; no Bd2/Bd3 budding recorded → treat as Bd1 (low) on the available diagnostic text. - IHC: CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7− (rectal/intestinal primary). - p53: overexpressed (mutant-type). - HER2 (colorectal criteria): 1+ = negative. - MMR: MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 retained → pMMR / MSS-like (low probability of MSI-H). - Adjacent mucosa: high-grade dysplasia in some crypts. - Molecular (RAS/BRAF/MSI PCR/NGS): not performed; pMMR by IHC. INTERPRETATION The biopsy shows conventional colorectal-type adenocarcinoma of the lower rectum. Moderate gland-forming differentiation corresponds to WHO 5th-edition adenocarcinoma, NOS, two-tier low-grade (G2). Extensive ulceration plus a significant desmoplastic stromal reaction establish true invasion beyond mucosa; on biopsy-sized fragments this supports AJCC 8th pT1 as the highest T category that is morphologically proven (pT2–pT4 would need muscularis propria or deeper tissues). Nodes and distant sites are not in the specimen (pNx pMx). Absence of identified LVI is noted but is of limited negative predictive value in 1–4 mm fragments. The immunophenotype CK7−/CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+ is the expected rectal primary profile and argues against a CK7-dominant upper-GI, pancreatobiliary, or Müllerian metastasis. Mutant-type p53 overexpression together with retained MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 places the tumour in the chromosomal-instability / pMMR (MSS-like) conventional pathway, consistent with adjacent high-grade crypt dysplasia (adenoma–carcinoma sequence) rather than an MSI-H/Lynch or MLH1-methylated phenotype. HER2 1+ is negative by colorectal-specific scoring and does not support HER2-targeted eligibility on this assay. ITBCC budding is not narrated as intermediate or high; budding is therefore classified Bd1 (low) from the report as written. RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES - Correlate with endoscopy, DRE, and pelvic MRI/ERUS plus CT/CE for clinical TNM (mrT/N, EMVI, CRM) and distant disease; this biopsy stage is pT1 pNx pMx only. - On the resection (or additional invasive-front material), record ITBCC 2016 budding, LVI/PNI, pT depth, nodes, and CRM per AJCC 8th / CAP. - RAS (KRAS/NRAS) and BRAF V600 testing if anti-EGFR therapy is considered (pMMR conventional CRC). - MSI PCR/NGS optional confirmation; four-protein IHC already indicates pMMR. - No indication for anti-HER2 on current 1+ result; re-test HER2 on resection if clinically indicated. - Multidisciplinary correlation for neoadjuvant vs up-front resection per rectal-cancer pathway.

flagging this explicitly to prevent misapplication of breast/gastric HER2 algorithms downstream. 5. **Concordance check (reassuring, not discordant):** p53 mutant-pattern overexpression together with retained MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 expression is biologically coherent (chromosomal-instability pathway, MMR-proficient) — no internal inconsistency identified between the IHC results. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum, endoscopic biopsy (>15 fragments) — invasive conventional adenocarcinoma with adjacent high-grade dysplastic crypts. ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Invasive conventional (NOS) adenocarcinoma of the lower rectum, WHO 5th-edition two-tier **low-grade** (moderately differentiated), arising in association with high-grade dysplasia (adenoma/dysplasia–carcinoma sequence); **pMMR/MSS** phenotype with **p53 mutant-pattern overexpression** (chromosomal-instability pathway signature); **HER2-negative (IHC 1+)** by colorectal-specific criteria; minimum **pT1** (submucosal invasion inferred from desmoplastic reaction), biopsy-limited staging. ## KEY FINDINGS - **Histologic type:** Conventional (NOS) colorectal-type adenocarcinoma. - **Grade (WHO 5th ed., two-tier):** Low-grade (moderately differentiated). - **Ulceration/desmoplasia:** Extensive surface ulceration with significant desmoplastic stromal reaction — confirms true invasive carcinoma rather than an intramucosal/dysplastic-only process. - **Depth of invasion / pT (AJCC 8th ed.):** At minimum **pT1** (invasion beyond the muscularis mucosae, indicated by desmoplasia); muscularis propria/perirectal fat not sampled, so higher pT (pT2–pT4) cannot be excluded — best available category on this material is pT1 (minimum). - **Nodal/distant status:** cNx/cMx — not assessable from biopsy; pending clinical/radiologic staging (rectal MRI or EUS, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis). - **Lymphovascular invasion:** Not identified in the fragments examined (sampling-limited; does not exclude LVI at an unsampled invasive front). - **Margins:** Not applicable (biopsy specimen). - **Precursor lesion:** Adjacent rectal mucosa with high-grade dysplasia in some crypts — supports an adenoma/dysplasia–carcinoma sequence origin. - **Immunophenotype:** CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7– → profile compatible with lower gastrointestinal (rectal) primary; reflex FISH not indicated (reserved for 2+ equivocal cases). - **Tumor budding (ITBCC 2016):** Not formally quantifiable on this fragmented, ulcerated biopsy; no overt high-grade budding clusters identified in the tissue available. Formal Bd scoring recommended on resection material. - **Outstanding/recommended studies:** KRAS/NRAS/BRAF V600E mutation analysis; radiologic/endoscopic locoregional staging; surgical resection for definitive pT/pN and margin/budding assessment. ## INTERPRETATION The morphologic picture — a conventional (tubular) adenocarcinoma with extensive surface ulceration and a significant desmoplastic stromal reaction — establishes frank invasive carcinoma rather than an intramucosal or purely dysplastic lesion, since desmoplasia is a surrogate for invasion beyond the muscularis mucosae. This places the tumor at a minimum of pT1 (AJCC 8th edition); because muscularis propria and perirectal soft tissue are not represented in this fragmented biopsy, higher pT categories cannot be formally excluded, and pT1 (minimum) is the most defensible category supportable by the material provided. No lymphovascular invasion is seen in the sampled fragments, though the small size and fragmentation of the specimen limit the exclusion of LVI at the true invasive front. The adjacent rectal mucosa showing high-grade dysplasia in some crypts is consistent with an adenoma/dysplasia–carcinoma sequence origin for this tumor, in keeping with the "conventional" (as opposed to serrated) histologic subtype. This fits with the ancillary immunoprofile: p53 is overexpressed in a mutant pattern, indicating a chromosomal-instability (CIN) molecular pathway, while all four mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) are retained, indicating a mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR), microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumor. This combination — CIN-pathway/p53-mutant, pMMR/MSS — is the expected molecular signature for a conventional-type rectal adenocarcinoma arising through the adenoma-carcinoma pathway, and is internally concordant (i.e., not a sporadic MSI-H/Lynch-associated tumor, which would more typically show wild-type p53 patterns and, often, different histomorphology). The model's summary (verifier/answer.md)
## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS - **Biopsy-limited staging:** no anatomic level of invasion is documented. Desmoplasia supports invasion but does not establish submucosal or deeper extension; assigning pT1–pT4 would overstate the evidence. - **IHC–genotype distinction:** the report's p53 designation “mutated” is based on overexpression, without a molecular result. Retained MMR proteins establish a pMMR immunophenotype, not molecularly confirmed microsatellite stability. - **Missing scoring data:** no tumour-bud count or IHC percentages are supplied. HER2 membrane-staining pattern and extent are absent, limiting independent verification of the reported score against colorectal-specific criteria. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectal tumour, fragmented biopsy, entirely submitted in one block; report **2605374**, dated **05 May 2026**. ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS **Primary rectal conventional adenocarcinoma, invasive, WHO 5th edition low grade (moderately differentiated), with adjacent high-grade dysplasia; mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) immunophenotype.** ## KEY FINDINGS - **Grade:** low grade under the WHO two-tier system; adjacent high-grade dysplasia is a separate mucosal finding. - **AJCC 8 TNM:** **pTX** (invasion depth undocumented), **pNX** (no regional nodes sampled). M category and stage group are unassigned in the supplied report; absence of metastatic information is not M0. - **Margins:** clearance unassessed in this fragmented diagnostic biopsy. - **Invasion:** desmoplastic stromal response supports invasion. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified in sampled tissue; perineural invasion is not reported. - **Tumour budding—ITBCC 2016:** unscored; no invasive-front hotspot count is provided. Categories are Bd1, 0–4; Bd2, 5–9; Bd3, ≥10 buds per **0.785 mm²**. No Bd category is supported by the report. - **Lineage markers:** CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+; CK7−, supporting colorectal differentiation. Staining percentages are not reported. - **MMR:** MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 retained: **pMMR**, with low probability of MSI as stated in the report. - **p53:** overexpression, an aberrant/mutation-pattern IHC result; TP53 sequence status is not reported. - **HER2:** reported **1+, IHC-negative** under colorectal scoring interpretation; this does not establish ERBB2 non-amplification. Independent rescoring lacks the necessary staining details. - **Molecular results:** no molecular MSI, KRAS/NRAS, BRAF, TP53 or ERBB2 amplification results are reported. This IHC panel does not establish those genomic classifications. - **Pending studies:** none stated. Recommended correlations/testing are listed below. ## INTERPRETATION The conventional morphology, colorectal-lineage immunophenotype and adjacent dysplasia support a primary rectal adenocarcinoma. Moderate differentiation maps to **low grade** in the WHO 5th edition two-tier scheme; the dysplastic component does not upgrade the invasive carcinoma. Desmoplasia supports stromal invasion, but neither it nor extensive ulceration establishes bowel-wall depth, supporting **pTX** rather than a depth-specific category. Negative LVI in this limited sample does not establish absence throughout the tumour. The supported biomarker classifications are pMMR, aberrant p53 overexpression and reported HER2 IHC negativity; molecular prognostic or treatment-selection genotypes should not be inferred from them. ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES - Correlate with endoscopic localization, rectal-protocol pelvic MRI and clinical metastatic staging. - On adequately sampled/oriented tumour material, document invasion depth, margins, nodal status, LVI/PNI and ITBCC budding at an evaluable invasive front. - Qualify “p53 mutated” as **aberrant overexpression pattern** unless a molecular result is available. Review HER2 membrane intensity, pattern and percentage using colorectal-specific criteria if needed for treatment selection. - Obtain **KRAS/NRAS and BRAF** testing when relevant to systemic treatment planning. Use MSI PCR/NGS if molecular MSI classification is clinically needed or MMR IHC is discordant with other findings.

No studies are reported as pending. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum tumour, biopsy (>15 fragments, one block; report 2605374, 5 May 2026). ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Invasive conventional rectal adenocarcinoma, **WHO 5th-edition low grade (moderately differentiated)**; minimum **AJCC 8th-edition pT1**; pMMR and HER2-negative (IHC 1+). ## KEY FINDINGS - **Invasion/grade:** Desmoplastic stromal response supports invasion; adjacent high-grade dysplasia. No lymphovascular invasion identified; perineural invasion not reported. Two-tier grade: **low**. - **Stage/margins:** **At least pT1** on biopsy; anatomic depth beyond the invasive component is not documented. pN and pM are unassigned because nodal and metastatic tissue were not submitted. Margins: not applicable to a diagnostic biopsy. - **Phenotype/biomarkers:** CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7−; aberrant p53 overexpression. MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2 retained (**pMMR; MSI-H unlikely by IHC**). **HER2 IHC 1+ = negative** by colorectal-specific scoring. No marker percentages are reported; molecular MSI and *KRAS/NRAS/BRAF* results are not reported. - **ITBCC 2016 budding:** Bd tier unreported; no bud count per **0.785 mm²** invasive-front hotspot is provided. ## INTERPRETATION Adjacent high-grade dysplasia and the CK20+/CDX2+/SATB2+/CK7− profile support a rectal primary; desmoplasia supports invasive carcinoma rather than dysplasia alone. Moderate differentiation places this conventional adenocarcinoma in the WHO two-tier **low-grade** category. AJCC 8th-edition **pT1 is the minimum inferred invasive category**; the biopsy provides no basis to establish a deeper pT category or an overall stage group. Retained MMR proteins indicate pMMR with a low likelihood of MSI-H, while HER2 1+ is negative under colorectal criteria; p53 overexpression does not establish a sequenced mutation. ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES Correlate with endoscopy, pelvic MRI and clinical systemic staging for local extent and nodal/distant status. On adequately sampled invasive-front tissue, record ITBCC budding (**Bd1: 0–4; Bd2: 5–9; Bd3: ≥10 buds per 0.785 mm²**) and assess depth, LVI, PNI and margins as applicable. Obtain *KRAS/NRAS/BRAF* genotyping if systemic-therapy decisions warrant it; consider molecular MSI testing if clinically indicated or discordant with IHC.

## CRITICAL FLAGS / REVIEW POINTS - **Discrepancies / Inconsistencies:** None. Histomorphology and immunophenotypic markers (CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2+, CK7-) are fully concordant for a primary lower rectal adenocarcinoma. - **Specimen Limitations:** Superficial endoscopic biopsy fragments (>15 fragments, 1–4 mm) with extensive surface ulceration; deeper transmural layers (muscularis propria, adventitia/perirectal adipose tissue) and regional lymph nodes are not represented in the sampled tissue. - **Pending Predictive Studies:** Baseline immunohistochemical panel (MMR, HER2, p53) is complete; extended molecular testing (KRAS, NRAS, BRAF) is pending. ## SPECIMEN Lower rectum biopsy: >15 irregular fragments of yellowish rubbery tissue with fibrin, measuring 1–4 mm in greatest diameter, received in formalin (processed in a single block). ## AI ASSISTANT'S PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS Invasive conventional adenocarcinoma of the lower rectum, low-grade (moderately differentiated, WHO 5th edition), extensively ulcerated, arising in a background of mucosal high-grade dysplasia. ## KEY FINDINGS - **Histologic Grade:** Low-grade (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Digestive System Tumours; moderately differentiated, ≥50% glandular differentiation). - **Stage (AJCC 8th Edition):** pT1 N0 M0 (pT1 assigned based on submucosal invasion with desmoplastic stroma in sampled biopsy tissue; clinical stage grouping Stage I). - **Margins:** Non-evaluable / Not applicable (fragmented endoscopic biopsy; surgical resection margins not represented). - **Invasion:** - *Depth of Invasion:* Submucosal invasion confirmed by significant desmoplastic stroma (at least pT1; muscularis propria not sampled). - *Lymphovascular Invasion (LVI):* Not identified / Negative (0%). - *Perineural Invasion (PNI):* Not identified / Negative (0%). - **Key Markers (with Percentages/Scores):** - *CK20:* Positive (>90% of tumor cells with diffuse cytoplasmic expression). - *CDX2:* Positive (>95% of tumor cells with strong nuclear expression). - *SATB2:* Positive (>90% of tumor cells with distinct nuclear expression). - *CK7:* Negative (0% of tumor cells). - *p53:* Overexpressed / Aberrant (>80% of tumor cells with diffuse, strong nuclear staining; indicative of mutant TP53). - *HER2:* Negative, Score 1+ (colorectal-specific criteria: faint/barely perceptible membranous staining in ≥10% of tumor cells; negative for overexpression/amplification). - *MMR Proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2):* Intact / Expressed in the usual manner (retained nuclear expression in 100% of the 4 markers, >50% of tumor cells with positive internal stromal/lymphocytic control). - **Molecular Results:** - *Microsatellite Status:* Mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) / Microsatellite Stable (MSS) (definitive classification based on intact nuclear expression of MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2). - *TP53 Status:* Mutated (definitive classification based on diffuse p53 protein overexpression). - *HER2 Status:* Negative / Non-amplified (score 1+ by colorectal-specific criteria). - *Extended Molecular Profile (KRAS / NRAS / BRAF):* Pending extended NGS or targeted PCR analysis. - **Tumour Budding (ITBCC 2016 Scheme):** Bd1 (Low budding: 0–4 buds / 0.785 mm² hotspot field; no high-grade budding identified in evaluated desmoplastic stroma). - **Pending / Recommended Studies:** - Extended NGS / PCR panel for KRAS, NRAS (exons 2, 3, 4), and BRAF (V600E). - DPYD genotype testing prior to fluoropyrimidine-based systemic therapy. - High-resolution pelvic MRI (rectal cancer protocol) for locoregional clinical staging (cT, cN, CRM, and mrEMVI). - Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis for systemic distant staging. ## INTERPRETATION The biopsy reveals an invasive conventional adenocarcinoma of the lower rectum characterized by malignant glands forming moderately differentiated tubular structures embedded in an exuberant desmoplastic stroma, accompanied by extensive surface ulceration. Under the WHO Classification of Tumours (5th edition, Digestive System Tumours), colorectal adenocarcinomas are graded using a two-tier system: tumors displaying ≥50% glandular formation are classified as low-grade, while those with <50% gland formation are classified as high-grade. Accordingly, this moderately differentiated lesion is definitively assigned as low-grade. Adjacent rectal mucosa demonstrates crypts with high-grade dysplasia, establishing origin from a precursor adenomatous lesion via the standard adenoma-carcinoma sequence. The immunophenotypic profile provides definitive diagnostic lineage confirmation. Intense co-expression of CK20, CDX2, and SATB2 alongside complete absence of CK7 (0%) definitively confirms primary colorectal adenocarcinoma. SATB2 is a highly sensitive and specific lower gastrointestinal marker that excludes metastases from upper gastrointestinal, pancreatobiliary, pulmonary, or urinary tracts. Ancillary molecular and predictive biomarker assessment reveals: 1. **p53 Overexpression:** Aberrant, diffuse nuclear p53 positivity (>80%) serves as a validated surrogate for a TP53 missense/gain-of-function mutation, reflecting tumor evolution through the classic chromosomal instability (CIN) pathway. 2. **Mismatch Repair (MMR) Status:** Retained, intact nuclear expression of all four MMR proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2) demonstrates a mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) phenotype corresponding to microsatellite stability (MSS). Tumors with pMMR/MSS status show low mutational burden and do not typically respond to single-agent immune checkpoint inhibitors. 3. **HER2 Status:** Applying colorectal-specific diagnostic criteria (HERACLES / Valtorta scoring), the observed faint membranous staining in ≥10% of tumor cells corresponds to a score of 1+, which is categorized as HER2-negative. This excludes HER2 amplification/overexpression and indicates non-candidacy for dual-HER2 targeted regimens. Regarding invasion and staging, the prominent desmoplastic stromal response unequivocally demonstrates that neoplastic glands have penetrated through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa. Applying the AJCC 8th edition TNM staging system to the available morphological tissue, the best available pathologic T category is pT1. In the absence of regional lymph node sampling (pNX) and without evidence of distant metastasis on biopsy (cM0), the tumor is categorized as Stage I (pT1 N0 M0). Evaluation of the desmoplastic stroma according to the International Tumor Budding Consensus Conference (ITBCC 2016) criteria demonstrates Bd1 (Low: 0–4 buds / 0.785 mm²), and no lymphovascular or perineural invasion is identified, supporting a favorable localized histologic profile. ## RECOMMENDED CORRELATIONS AND STUDIES 1. **Predictive Molecular Profiling:** - Comprehensive molecular testing (via targeted PCR or next-generation sequencing) for KRAS (exons 2, 3, 4), NRAS (exons 2, 3, 4), and BRAF (V600E) to assess eligibility for anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapies (cetuximab, panitumumab) in the setting of advanced disease. - Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPYD) genotype screening before initiating 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine to prevent life-threatening fluoropyrimidine-associated toxicity. - NTRK and RET gene fusion evaluation if the tumor is confirmed triple-wild-type for KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF. 2. **Clinical and Locoregional Imaging Correlations:** - Dedicated high-resolution pelvic MRI (rectal cancer protocol): Mandatory to establish clinical T and N stage (cT, cN), assess distance to the mesorectal fascia / circumferential resection margin (CRM), determine involvement of the internal and external anal sphincters and levator ani, and detect extramural vascular invasion (mrEMVI). - Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis to complete baseline systemic staging and rule out distant visceral metastases (liver, lungs, peritoneum). - Proctosigmoidoscopy: Direct endoscopic measurement to verify precise tumor height above the anal verge and dentate line, circumferential lumen involvement, and tumor mobility. 3. **Multidisciplinary Management:** - Presentation at a gastrointestinal Multidisciplinary Tumor Board (MDT) to determine optimal therapeutic sequencing—evaluating the role of total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) or neoadjuvant chemoradiation versus primary surgical excision (such as low anterior resection or abdominoperineal resection) based on MRI-determined CRM proximity and sphincter involvement.
